Summary: Active Admin — Promo Code admin tool: fix 2 bugs (Value save, auto-expire), 3 UX consolidations, and add Category scoping + platform-subsidised "Add Money to Request" Type
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher admin managing Promo Codes,

## 🎯 I want

the Promo Code admin tool to work reliably, present a cleaner UI, and support category scoping plus a new platform-subsidised promo type,

## ✅ So that

I can configure codes correctly the first time, without working around bugs, and can run more targeted marketing campaigns including Gopher Rewards.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

This ticket bundles seven distinct improvements to the existing Promo Code admin tool. They are split into bugs (must fix), UX consolidations (clean up the existing screen), and feature additions. All seven land on the same screen and are best shipped together, but each is independently scoped below for clarity.

---

## 📋 The 7 Improvements

| # | Type | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | UX | **Applies To** — remove the "Applies To" selector entirely. Only Requestors submit requests, so the field has a single possible value and is redundant; all codes are requestor-only. |
| 2 | Feature | **Type** — add a new option for a **platform-subsidised promo** that adds money to the request budget. |
| 3 | Bug | **Value** — fix the bug where the value field intermittently fails to save (both $ and % variants). |
| 4 | UX | **Reduces tab merge** — combine "Reduces" and "Reduces On Age Restricted Fee" into a single tab with **multi-select checkboxes** (Gopher Fee, Instant Transfer Fee, Age-Restricted Fee) plus a **Select All** shortcut. A code can reduce one or more fees. |
| 5 | UX | **Duration** — remove the "once" option (already asked at the top of the page). |
| 6 | Feature | **Categories** — add ability to scope a promo code to specific request categories using checkboxes plus a Select All shortcut. |
| 7 | Bug | **Auto-expire** — codes must become inactive precisely at their expiration timestamp. Doesn't work today. |

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior — Per Item

### Item 1 — Remove the "Applies To" selector

* The "Applies To" selector is removed from the Promo Code admin screen entirely. Requestors are the only parties who submit requests, so the field has a single possible value and is redundant; every code is implicitly requestor-only.
* This supersedes the original ask of only removing the "Gophers" option — since Requestors is the sole remaining target, the whole selector is dropped rather than left as a one-option field. **Dev note: remove the field; do not ship a single-option dropdown.**
* Any existing codes that have "Gophers" set should be reviewed by admin; one-time migration is out of scope but those codes effectively become inert.

### Item 2 — New "Add Money to Request" Type

* Add a new Type option to the existing Type selector (alongside the existing reductive types).
* **Effect:** the Requestor's checkout total is reduced by the promo amount, while the **Gopher's payout is preserved in full**. The platform absorbs the difference.
* This is the foundation for Gopher Rewards / marketplace-incentive campaigns where the platform pays to attract demand without shorting the Gopher.
* The Value field, Duration, and Categories selectors all apply to this Type the same way they apply to existing types.
* The accounting impact (platform-side ledger entry recording the subsidy per redemption) needs to be captured so it can be reconciled.

### Item 3 — Fix the Value save bug

* The Value field must reliably persist whatever the admin entered (dollar amount or percentage), without requiring a second edit.
* Both $ amount and % off variants must save and reload identically to what was entered.
* Identify and fix the underlying cause — do not work around it with a client-side retry.

### Item 4 — Merge "Reduces" tabs into one multi-select

* Today there are two tabs: "Reduces" and "Reduces On Age Restricted Fee."
* Merge into a single tab listing the three fees a code can reduce:

    * Gopher Fee
    * Instant Transfer Fee
    * Age-Restricted Fee
    
* Use **checkboxes** for multi-select — a code can reduce one OR MORE of these — plus a **Select All** shortcut that toggles all three on or off. At least one fee must be selected.
* At redemption, the discount applies to the combined total of the selected fees.
* Migrate existing codes: a code currently set against the Age-Restricted Fee loads with the Age-Restricted Fee box pre-checked; everything else with the appropriate box(es) checked.
* **Note:** updated from the original single-select / radio design to multi-select checkboxes + Select All (product decision). See Implementation Considerations.

### Item 5 — Remove redundant Duration "once"

* Remove the "once" option from the Duration selector. This option is already covered by a question asked at the top of the page, and having it in Duration creates redundant configuration.
* Migrate existing codes: any code currently set to Duration = once should be migrated to the equivalent state via the top-of-page question.

### Item 6 — Category selection

* Add a new field to scope a promo code to specific request categories.
* Categories available: **Delivery**, **Ride Sharing**, **Service**, **Other**.
* Use **checkboxes** for multi-select (a code can apply to one or more categories), plus a **Select All** shortcut that toggles every checkbox on or off.
* At redemption, the code is only valid if the order's request type falls within the selected categories. If no categories are selected, the code is invalid (admin must explicitly choose at least one, or Select All).

### Item 7 — Fix auto-expire

* When a code's expiration date / timestamp passes, the code must become inactive **precisely at that timestamp**, not on a deferred sweep.
* The check must run at the moment of redemption (server-side validation) so the timing is exact regardless of any background job cadence.
* Already-redeemed-before-expiration usages remain valid; only future redemptions are blocked.
* Active/inactive state displayed in the admin UI should reflect the live evaluation (active until expiration timestamp, inactive thereafter).

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Applies To selector removed**

* **Given** an admin opens the Promo Code create / edit screen,
* **When** they view the form,
* **Then** there is no "Applies To" selector at all (and therefore no "Gophers" option); codes are requestor-only by default.

**Scenario 2 — New Add Money to Request Type works**

* **Given** an admin creates a promo code with the new Type and a value of $5,
* **When** a Requestor redeems it on a request with a $20 budget,
* **Then** the Requestor's checkout total is reduced by $5, and the Gopher's payout on the resulting order is unchanged from what it would have been at the original $20 budget.

**Scenario 3 — Platform subsidy is captured in the ledger**

* **Given** the new Type code is redeemed,
* **When** the resulting transactions are recorded,
* **Then** a platform-side ledger entry captures the subsidy amount so it can be reconciled in financial reporting.

**Scenario 4 — Value field saves correctly**

* **Given** an admin enters a dollar amount in the Value field,
* **When** they save the code,
* **Then** the code reloads with the exact value entered — no need to re-edit.

**Scenario 5 — Value field works for percentages too**

* **Given** an admin enters a percentage in the Value field,
* **When** they save the code,
* **Then** the code reloads with the exact percentage entered.

**Scenario 6 — Reduces tabs are merged into one multi-select**

* **Given** an admin opens the Promo Code edit screen,
* **When** they view the Reduces section,
* **Then** they see a single section with three fee checkboxes (Gopher Fee, Instant Transfer Fee, Age-Restricted Fee) plus a Select All shortcut — not two separate tabs — and can select one or more. At least one fee is required.

**Scenario 7 — Existing Age-Restricted codes migrate cleanly**

* **Given** an admin opens a code that was previously configured against the Age-Restricted Fee tab,
* **When** the new merged UI loads it,
* **Then** the Age-Restricted Fee checkbox is pre-checked with no data loss.

**Scenario 8 — Duration "once" option is removed**

* **Given** an admin opens the Promo Code create / edit screen,
* **When** they view the Duration selector,
* **Then** "once" is no longer an option.

**Scenario 9 — Category multi-select with Select All works**

* **Given** an admin is configuring a new code,
* **When** they tick the Delivery and Ride Sharing checkboxes,
* **Then** the code is scoped to those categories. Tapping Select All ticks all four (Delivery, Ride Sharing, Service, Other); tapping it again unticks all.

**Scenario 10 — Category scoping enforced at redemption**

* **Given** a code scoped to Delivery only,
* **When** a Requestor attempts to redeem it on a Ride Sharing request,
* **Then** redemption is rejected with a clear "not valid for this request type" message.

**Scenario 11 — Auto-expire is precise**

* **Given** a code's expiration timestamp is 5:00 PM today,
* **When** a Requestor attempts redemption at 5:00:01 PM,
* **Then** redemption is rejected with an "expired" message — no sweep-job delay.

**Scenario 12 — Already-redeemed usages stay valid after expiration**

* **Given** a Requestor redeemed a code before its expiration timestamp,
* **When** that order is processed after the expiration timestamp,
* **Then** the order continues to honour the discount — expiration affects only future redemptions.

**Scenario 13 — Active / inactive display reflects live state**

* **Given** the admin views a code in the Promo Code list view,
* **When** the code's expiration timestamp passes,
* **Then** the list view shows the code as inactive without requiring a page refresh or admin action.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* The new "Add Money to Request" Type **must preserve the Gopher's payout in full**. The discount is absorbed by the platform, not the Gopher.
* Every redemption of the new Type must produce a ledger entry recording the platform's subsidy for that order.
* Promo code expiration is evaluated **at redemption time, server-side**. No deferred sweeps.
* Category selection requires at least one category to be selected (or Select All); a code with zero categories is invalid.
* The Reduces tab merge does not change which fee(s) a given code reduces — existing codes migrate to the equivalent checkbox selection. A code may now reduce more than one fee; at least one fee is required.
* The Value field fix must address the root cause, not be a client-side workaround.
* The Applies To selector is removed entirely; codes are persisted as requestor-only. Existing codes with "Gophers" set become effectively inert (no migration of those codes is in scope).

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* The two bugs (Value save, auto-expire) likely live in separate code paths from the UI changes. Worth investigating early so any required backend changes are scoped before UI work begins.
* The new "Add Money to Request" Type touches multiple subsystems: promo-code redemption, order pricing, Gopher payout calculation, and platform accounting. Recommend mapping each subsystem and identifying the single source of truth for "Gopher payout amount" before changing anything.
* Auto-expire at redemption time is the right call for precision, but admin-side list views also need a way to display the current active/inactive state. The simplest implementation: compute active/inactive on the fly based on `expires_at <= now()` whenever the code is read.
* For category selection, consider whether existing codes (created before this feature) default to "all categories" or to a specific subset. Recommended default: all categories (matches today's behaviour where there was no category restriction).
* **(Updated) Reduces is multi-select** — checkboxes + Select All, not the single-select radio originally drafted. A code can reduce one or more fees and redemption discounts the combined total of the selected fees. Data model: `reducesFees: string[]` (legacy single-value `reducesFee` is normalized to an array on read). At least one fee is required.
* **(Updated) Applies To selector removed entirely** — not left as a single-option ("Requestors") dropdown. Codes are persisted as requestor-only.
* Recommend deploying behind a feature flag covering the new Type and the new Category selector. The bug fixes and UX consolidations can ship unflagged once tested.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Walk through every Scenario above explicitly — each maps to one of the 7 improvements.
* For the Value bug: create and save dozens of codes with varying $ and % values and reload each. The bug is intermittent today, so volume matters.
* For auto-expire: set a test code to expire in 60 seconds, wait, and confirm redemption fails. Repeat with millisecond precision boundaries to be sure.
* For the new Type: confirm both the Requestor checkout total and the Gopher payout against an order baseline that's been recorded before promo application.
* For the Reduces merge: open existing codes from both old tabs and confirm they load correctly under the new single multi-select section; confirm Select All toggles all three fees, that a code can reduce more than one fee, and that the redemption discount equals the combined total of the selected fees.
* For the Duration removal: open existing codes with Duration = once and confirm they have been migrated to the equivalent top-of-page state.
* Run on both the production-like staging environment and confirm against a Stripe test mode — the new Type's subsidy ledger entry must be visible in the test ledger.

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* The new "Add Money to Request" Type is the foundation for **Gopher Rewards**, which is a forthcoming feature. Once this Type exists, marketing can run subsidised campaigns; the larger Gopher Rewards configuration is out of scope here.
* Depends on the existing Promo Code redemption pipeline being modifiable to support the platform-subsidised payout path.
* Out of scope: backfill / migration of existing codes that have "Gophers" set in Applies To. They become inert; admin can manually remove them if desired.
* Out of scope: any Requestor-facing UI changes (e.g., showing the promo savings on checkout). This ticket is admin-tool only — once a code is configured, the existing Requestor redemption UI is assumed to consume it correctly.

Summary: Both apps — Add Deleted tab to Inbox with swipe-left-to-delete, permanent-delete confirmation, 90-day auto-purge, and admin-expiration auto-move
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

User of either app (Gopher Request / Gopher Go) managing my in-app Inbox,

## 🎯 I want

to delete messages with a swipe-left gesture and review removed messages in a dedicated Deleted tab before they are permanently gone,

## ✅ So that

I can keep my Inbox tidy with a familiar texting-app gesture while still having a brief safety window to recover or permanently remove messages on my own terms.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* The in-app Inbox should feel like a standard mobile texting experience. Today there is no way for a user to delete messages from the Inbox.
* This ticket introduces a **two-stage delete** pattern:

    1. **Swipe left on a message in the Inbox** moves it to a new **Deleted** tab.
    2. **Delete from the Deleted tab** is the **permanent** delete — confirmed by a pop-up so an inadvertent tap can be aborted.
    
* The **"silence"** feature commonly seen on similar UIs is **not** part of this scope.
* Admin-sent messages that have an expiration date attached **auto-move from Inbox to Deleted** at the expiration date/time. They then follow the same rules as any other message in the Deleted tab.
* This work applies to **both apps** — Gopher Request and Gopher Go.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

### Inbox tab

* A user can **swipe left** on any message in the Inbox to move it to the Deleted tab.
* No silence affordance is added.

### Deleted tab

* A new **Deleted** tab is added to the Inbox view.
* Messages in the Deleted tab can only be **permanently deleted** — there is no "restore to Inbox" affordance in this release.
* Attempting to delete a message from the Deleted tab triggers a confirmation pop-up so an inadvertent swipe/tap can be aborted.
* Messages in the Deleted tab are **automatically purged after 90 days** measured from when they entered the Deleted tab.

### Admin expiration handling

* When an admin sends a message with an expiration date, that message **auto-moves from Inbox to Deleted at the expiration date/time**.
* Once in the Deleted tab, the admin message follows the same rules as any other deleted message — it can be manually permanently deleted by the user, and it auto-purges after 90 days.

---

## 💰 Confirmation Pop-up (default copy)

* **Title:** Delete permanently?
* **Body:** This cannot be undone.
* **Buttons:** Cancel (secondary) / Delete (primary destructive)
* Pull final copy from Figma if defined there — the above is a sensible default that gives the user the abort path you asked for.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Swipe-left moves a message from Inbox to Deleted**

* **Given** a user is viewing the Inbox tab,
* **When** the user swipes left on a message,
* **Then** the message is removed from the Inbox and appears in the Deleted tab.

**Scenario 2 — No restore from Deleted to Inbox**

* **Given** a message is in the Deleted tab,
* **When** the user views the message in the Deleted tab,
* **Then** there is no "restore to Inbox" option — the only actions are read and permanent delete.

**Scenario 3 — Permanent delete from Deleted requires confirmation**

* **Given** a user is viewing the Deleted tab,
* **When** the user attempts to delete a message from that tab,
* **Then** a confirmation pop-up appears with the copy above and the user must tap Delete to proceed (Cancel aborts and leaves the message in place).

**Scenario 4 — 90-day auto-purge from Deleted**

* **Given** a message has been in the Deleted tab for 90 days,
* **When** the auto-purge runs,
* **Then** the message is permanently removed from the Deleted tab without further user action.

**Scenario 5 — Admin-sent message with expiration auto-moves to Deleted**

* **Given** an admin sent a message with an expiration date/time and the message is currently in the user's Inbox,
* **When** the expiration date/time is reached,
* **Then** the message automatically moves from Inbox to Deleted.

**Scenario 6 — Admin-expired messages follow the same Deleted-tab rules**

* **Given** an admin-sent message has been auto-moved to the Deleted tab,
* **When** the user views the Deleted tab,
* **Then** the message can be manually permanently deleted (with confirmation) and otherwise auto-purges 90 days after it entered the Deleted tab.

**Scenario 7 — Swipe-left silence affordance is NOT present**

* **Given** the feature has shipped,
* **When** a user swipes left on a message in the Inbox,
* **Then** no "silence" option appears — only the delete action.

**Scenario 8 — Both apps covered**

* **Given** the fix has shipped,
* **When** a user opens either Gopher Request or Gopher Go,
* **Then** the Deleted tab, swipe-left-to-delete, confirmation pop-up, 90-day purge, and admin-expiration auto-move all behave the same in both apps.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* Deletion is **two-stage**: swipe-left moves Inbox → Deleted; explicit delete from the Deleted tab permanently removes.
* The permanent-delete action **must** be confirmed by a pop-up so accidental taps can be aborted.
* Messages in the Deleted tab **auto-purge after 90 days** regardless of how they got there (user swipe or admin expiration).
* No "restore to Inbox" affordance is in scope for this release.
* No "silence" affordance is in scope for this release.
* Admin-sent messages with expiration dates auto-move from Inbox to Deleted at their expiration time. Once in Deleted, they follow the same rules as any other deleted message.
* The Deleted tab is part of the Inbox view in **both** apps — Gopher Request and Gopher Go.

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* The 90-day auto-purge requires a background job (or a check-on-fetch in the Inbox API) that evaluates `deleted_at` timestamps and permanently removes records older than 90 days. Each Deleted-tab record must carry a `deleted_at` timestamp.
* Admin-expiration auto-move likewise requires either a scheduled job or an on-fetch check evaluating the admin message's `expires_at` and moving it.
* The two background processes can share the same job runner.
* The Deleted tab should still allow the user to **open and read** a message before deciding to permanently delete it.
* The Figma reference for visual design and pop-up styling is included in the description — follow that strictly for spacing, copy, and button order.

---

## 🎨 Design Reference

* **Figma:** https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=107-15594

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Swipe-left on an Inbox message and confirm it appears in the Deleted tab and is gone from Inbox.
* Delete a message from the Deleted tab and confirm the pop-up appears; tap Cancel and confirm the message remains; tap Delete and confirm the message is gone.
* Place a message in Deleted, fast-forward (or test-data manipulate) the `deleted_at` timestamp to 90+ days ago, and confirm the auto-purge removes it.
* Send a test admin message with a near-future expiration date, confirm it sits in Inbox until expiration, then verify it auto-moves to Deleted.
* From the Deleted tab, manually delete an admin message and confirm the same confirmation flow runs.
* Confirm no "silence" affordance exists on swipe-left.
* Test on both iOS and Android.
* Test on both apps — Gopher Request and Gopher Go.
* Re-attach the two screenshots directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URLs do not render for other users).

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* The admin-message expiration date model must exist on the admin side and be readable by the apps. If that field is not currently exposed, that work is part of this scope.
* The 90-day auto-purge is permanent — there is no recovery once purged. This is consistent with the permanent-delete confirmation behavior and the no-restore design.
* Consider deploying behind a feature flag so the auto-purge job can be toggled if the threshold needs adjustment in production.

Summary: Gopher App - Expired Request - Email Update (1st Time Promo Code & Promo Code Already Used)
Description:
## Goal

When a Requestor's order **expires**, they receive the expired-request email carrying a **"ReDo" promo** — unless they've already used it:

* Has **not** used ReDo → email **with** the promo code.
* **Has** used ReDo → same email **without** the promo code.

## Decisions (John, 2026-07-03)

* **Shape:** an **update to the existing transactional expired email** (a conditional block) — not a separate drip send. Stays transactional (`support@`, no unsubscribe), dispatcher **type 17**.
* **ReDo mechanics:** **100% of Gopher fees waived → $0 fees on the next request, redeemable once per account.**
* **Timing:** "not in play until we start the Drip Campaign" — build now, ship behind an activation flag.

**▶ Full developer handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-104-expired-redo-promo.md` · impl detail: `Documentation/SMS:Emails/impl-expired-redo-promo-G40-104.md`

## ✅ Done (front-end) — `SMS:Emails/gopher-email-expired.html`

Conditional **ReDo promo card** authored directly above the "Relist your request" CTA, using the email's own design tokens (mint card, navy/green): eyebrow → **"Your next request is fee-free."** → "Relist with code **ReDo** and we'll waive every Gopher fee — you pay **$0 in fees**. One-time, our treat." → dashed **ReDo** chip. Commented with the render rule (shown only when the requestor hasn't redeemed ReDo; suppressed after). Verified in-browser; screenshot shared. Preview shows the block-present state; redeemed state = same email without the block.

## 🔧 To build (developer) — no new promo infra needed; reuses the `coupons` model

1. **Create the ReDo coupon** (`coupons` row): `code:'ReDo'`, `applies_to:'requestor'`, `type:'percentOff'`, `value:100`, `reduces:'gopherFee'`, `once_per_acct:true`, `duration:'once'`, `active:true`, `redeem_by:<campaign end>`. Existing `verify_coupon_use` → `get_discounted_rate` already zeroes the fee.
2. **Gate** — reuse the `once_per_acct` pattern in `controllers/order/coupon.js:50-55`: `SELECT id FROM orders WHERE coupon_id=:redo AND requestor_id=:user` → row exists ⇒ suppress block.
3. **Fire point** — expiry cron `middleware/crons.js:259` & `:278` (`send_mail(17, …)`): compute `showReDo`, pass `showReDo` + `redoCode` into `email_data` (second query must also select `o.requestor_id`).
4. **Template** — port the rebranded `gopher-email-expired` markup to the type-17 view (`lib/sendEmail.js:44`) and wrap the card in `<% if (showReDo) { %> … <% } %>`.
5. **Activation flag** — gate on `EXPIRED_REDO_ENABLED` (flip at drip-campaign go-live).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Expired email shows the **ReDo** code when the requestor has not used it; **omits** it once redeemed (once per account).
2. ReDo applies **100% off the Gopher fee** ($0 fees) on the next request.
3. Delivered as the transactional expired email (type 17), not a new drip send.
4. Not active until the drip campaign begins (activation flag).

Summary: Both apps — App-store review pre-prompt for engaged users (Request: ≥5 completed + opens History; Go: ≥7 completed in 7 days)
Description:
## Goal

Nudge engaged, happy users to leave a store review at a positive moment, using the **platform-native** review APIs (iOS `SKStoreReviewController`, Android Play In-App Review `ReviewManager`). A **branded pre-prompt gate** is shown first (“Rate us / Not now”); only on **Rate us** does the app call the native API — so we ask in our own voice and keep the native prompt for users who opt in. Applies to **both apps** (Request + Go).

> **Eligibility rewritten (John, 2026-07-02) — replaces the old 3-in-a-row + all-5-star logic:**
>
> * **Gopher Request (Requestor):** eligible when a user with **≥ 5 completed requests** opens **Request History**; the pre-prompt shows there.
> * **Gopher Go (Gopher):** eligible after **≥ 7 completed requests within a rolling 7-day window** — the real trigger fires **post-completion** when that threshold is crossed.
> 

**▶ Full developer handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-107-review-prompt.md`

## ✅ Done (front-end, verified in-browser)

* **Request web** (`Final/gopher-request.html`): branded `#reviewPromptOverlay` gate wired to open when **Request History** (`showSection('previous')`) opens and the user has **≥5 completed** requests; once per session. Copy: “Enjoying Gopher? … a quick App Store rating helps your neighbors find us.”
* **Gopher Go** (`Final/gopher-go.html`): branded `#goReviewOverlay` gate (dark theme) gated on a **≥7-completed-this-week** eligibility stub (dev replaces with the server’s rolling-7-day count); once per session. Copy: “Enjoy earning with Gopher Go? …”
* Both: **Rate us** swaps to a thank-you panel marking the native-API call seam; **Not now** dismisses. Demo helper `__previewReviewPrompt()`. Verified: gate fires only when eligible, once-guard holds, correct per-app copy + live counts, **zero console errors**; screenshots captured.

## 🔧 To build (developer / backend + native)

* **Native call** on Rate us: iOS `SKStoreReviewController.requestReview()` (scene-based on iOS 14+); Android Play In-App Review `ReviewManager`. OS renders its own prompt + enforces its own rate limit (iOS ≤ 3 / 365 days). **Do not track** the outcome — the APIs don’t expose it.
* **Server eligibility:** Request → lifetime completed-count ≥ 5; Go → rolling-7-day completed-count ≥ 7, computed post-completion, exposed as a `should_prompt_review` flag (replaces the Go stub).
* **Trigger wiring:** Request → on History open when eligible; Go → **after an order completes** when the 7-in-7 threshold is crossed (the prototype uses history-open only because a static page has no live completion event).
* **Feature flag** around the whole feature for rollback.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Request:** a Requestor with ≥ 5 completed requests opens Request History → the branded pre-prompt appears (once). On **Rate us** the app calls the native review API.
2. **Go:** a Gopher reaches ≥ 7 completed requests within 7 days → after that completion the branded pre-prompt appears. On **Rate us** the app calls the native review API.
3. **Native only:** no custom prompt bypasses the native APIs; the OS shows its own UI and enforces its own frequency limit.
4. **No tracking:** the app does not record whether the user left a review.
5. **Feature-flagged:** the whole feature can be toggled off.

_Superseded: the previous 3-consecutive-completions + only-5-star-ratings-given eligibility and its acceptance scenarios are obsolete._

Summary: Gopher Request — Send automated 48-hour check-in email to Requestor when a scheduled request is still un-accepted
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher Request operations system,

## 🎯 I want

to send an automated 48-hour check-in email to a Requestor whose scheduled request is still un-accepted,

## ✅ So that

the Requestor knows we are still working on finding them a Gopher, and — if they no longer need the service — has a one-tap path to cancel the request rather than letting it sit live indefinitely.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* A request that reaches the 48-hour mark un-accepted is, in practice, always a **scheduled** request — on-demand requests resolve (or expire) on a much shorter timeline.
* This email is a customer-care touchpoint: it reassures the Requestor that the platform is still actively trying to match them, and gives them a clear off-ramp if they have moved on (booked elsewhere, no longer need the service, etc.).
* The cancel path in the email uses the **existing deep link** into the Gopher Request app for that specific request, so the user lands directly on the request's cancel flow.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* **Trigger:** 48 hours after request **submission**, evaluated continuously.
* **Gate:** the email is sent **only if** the request is still active and un-accepted at the 48-hour mark.

    * If the request has been accepted, completed, or cancelled before 48 hours have elapsed, **no email is sent**.
    
* **Recipient:** the Requestor's email address on file for the account that submitted the request.
* **Channel:** email only (no SMS, no in-app notification as part of this ticket).
* **One-time:** each request triggers at most one 48-hour check-in email — no repeats.
* **Cancel link:** uses the existing Gopher Request app deep link that opens the specific request and routes the user to its cancel flow.

---

## 📧 Email Content (draft — confirm against existing email template style)

* **From:** the standard Gopher Request system address (e.g., `admin@gophergo.io` or whatever the existing email-from is for system messages).
* **To:** Requestor's email on file.
* **Subject:** Still need a Gopher? We're on it.

**Body (draft):**

Hi \[First Name\],

We're still working on matching you with a Gopher for your scheduled request. Sometimes scheduled requests take a little longer to find the right fit.

If you still need help, no action is needed — we'll keep working on it.

If your plans have changed and you no longer need a Gopher, you can cancel your request here:

\[**Open request in app**\] → _deep-link to the specific request's cancel flow in the Gopher Request app_

Thanks for using Gopher.

_— The Gopher Team_

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Email sent at 48 hours when request is still un-accepted**

* **Given** a scheduled request was submitted exactly 48 hours ago and is still in an active, un-accepted state,
* **When** the 48-hour check-in job runs,
* **Then** the check-in email is sent to the Requestor's email on file.

**Scenario 2 — No email if accepted before 48 hours**

* **Given** a request was accepted by a Gopher before the 48-hour mark,
* **When** the 48-hour check-in job evaluates that request,
* **Then** no email is sent.

**Scenario 3 — No email if cancelled before 48 hours**

* **Given** a request was cancelled before the 48-hour mark (by the Requestor or by an admin),
* **When** the 48-hour check-in job evaluates that request,
* **Then** no email is sent.

**Scenario 4 — No email if completed before 48 hours**

* **Given** a request was completed before the 48-hour mark,
* **When** the 48-hour check-in job evaluates that request,
* **Then** no email is sent.

**Scenario 5 — One email per request, ever**

* **Given** a request has already received its 48-hour check-in email,
* **When** the job runs again for that request,
* **Then** no additional email is sent — the check-in is a one-time send per request.

**Scenario 6 — Cancel link deep-links to the correct request**

* **Given** the Requestor receives the check-in email,
* **When** the Requestor taps the cancel link on a device with Gopher Request installed,
* **Then** the app opens to the specific request's cancel flow, not the home screen and not a different request.

**Scenario 7 — Email is sent from the standard system sender and lands in inbox**

* **Given** the email is generated,
* **When** it is dispatched,
* **Then** it is sent from the standard Gopher Request system email address and successfully delivers to the Requestor's inbox (passes SPF/DKIM, not flagged as spam in routine testing).

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* The 48-hour timer is anchored to **request submission**, not to the start of broadcasting (in case those can differ).
* The check-in email is sent **at most once** per request, regardless of subsequent state changes.
* The email only sends if the request is **active and un-accepted** at the moment of evaluation.
* The cancel link in the email **must** use the existing Gopher Request app deep link for that specific request — do not introduce a new web cancel flow.
* The email is **email-only** — no SMS or in-app duplication is in scope for this ticket.
* This is **not** part of a multi-step nurture sequence — it is a single check-in. (The original ticket's "Step 1" phrasing was an error.)

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* The 48-hour check requires either a scheduled job (e.g., hourly cron evaluating requests submitted \~48 hours ago) or per-request scheduled task created at submission time. Either approach is acceptable; the per-request scheduled task is more precise but adds operational overhead.
* A `48h_checkin_sent_at` (or similar) flag on the request record is needed to enforce the one-time send rule.
* The deep link should follow the existing format the app already supports for opening a specific request — reuse, don't reinvent.
* If the Requestor's email on file is missing or invalid, log the failure and move on. Do not block the request.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Submit a test request, fast-forward (or test-data manipulate) `submitted_at` to 48+ hours ago, run the check-in job, and confirm the email is sent.
* Repeat the above for a request that was accepted, cancelled, or completed before 48 hours — confirm no email is sent in each case.
* Run the check-in job twice against the same request and confirm only one email is sent.
* Tap the cancel link in the delivered email and confirm the Gopher Request app opens to that specific request's cancel flow.
* Test on both iOS and Android device email clients (Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook) to confirm the deep link behaves correctly on each.
* Confirm the email passes basic deliverability (SPF/DKIM, not flagged as spam on standard inboxes).

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* This ticket depends on the existing deep-link mechanism that opens the Gopher Request app to a specific request's cancel flow. If that deep link does not exist yet, that is in scope as a prerequisite.
* The system sender address and basic transactional email infrastructure are assumed to exist already (used elsewhere in the platform).

Summary: Active Admin — Capture Yes/No "Suggested Offer Used" on Delivery and Ride orders and surface in the Orders report + order detail view
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher operations team analysing pricing behaviour,

## 🎯 I want

the Orders report and order detail view in the Admin Panel to record whether each Delivery or Ride request used the Suggested Offer Assistance pricing flow,

## ✅ So that

we can validate — with real data — whether the suggested-pricing feature is materially influencing Requestor pricing decisions and whether to invest further in it.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* When a Requestor submits a Delivery or Ride request, they are shown the **Suggested Offer Assistance** modal containing a Low → Fair → Generous slider with a system-suggested amount.
* From that modal, the Requestor can either tap **SUBMIT** — which submits the request at whatever value the slider is currently on — or tap **BACK** to exit and enter their own price through a different flow.
* Today we have no way to distinguish, in our data, which Requestors submitted _through_ the Suggested Offer Assistance modal versus those who entered pricing through another path.
* Without that signal, we cannot answer the strategic question: is the pricing assistant actually influencing Requestor behaviour?

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* For every **Delivery** and **Ride Sharing** request submitted after this feature ships, capture a `suggested_offer_used` flag on the order record:

    * **Yes** — the Requestor submitted the request by tapping **SUBMIT** on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal (regardless of where they had moved the slider within the Low–Generous range).
    * **No** — the Requestor submitted the request through any other path (e.g., backed out of the assistance modal and entered a price elsewhere, or never opened the assistance modal).
    
* Surface this value in two places in the Admin Panel:

    * As a **new column** in the report generated from the **Orders** view (filterable / sortable / exportable).
    * As a **"Suggested Offer Used: Yes/No"** field on the **Order # detail view**.
    
* The flag is captured **going forward only** — existing orders submitted before this ships remain `null` / blank and are not back-filled.
* Request types other than Delivery and Ride Sharing are out of scope for this release — the field should be `null` / blank for those.

---

## 📊 Data Model (sketch)

* **Field name:** `suggested_offer_used` (or your existing naming convention equivalent).
* **Allowed values:** `true`, `false`, `null`.
* **Set to** `true` when: the request was submitted via the Suggested Offer Assistance modal's SUBMIT button.
* **Set to** `false` when: a Delivery or Ride request was submitted through any other path.
* **Set to** `null` when: the request is not a Delivery or Ride request, OR the order existed before this feature shipped (no backfill).
* **Immutable:** value is written once at submission and never changes thereafter.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Submit via Suggested Offer Assistance = Yes**

* **Given** a Requestor is creating a Delivery or Ride request,
* **When** they tap **SUBMIT** on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal (whether or not they moved the slider),
* **Then** the order record's `suggested_offer_used` value is `true` and displays as **Yes** in the Admin Panel.

**Scenario 2 — Back out of the modal then submit elsewhere = No**

* **Given** a Requestor opens the Suggested Offer Assistance modal,
* **When** they tap **BACK** and then submit the request through a different pricing path,
* **Then** the order record's `suggested_offer_used` value is `false` and displays as **No** in the Admin Panel.

**Scenario 3 — Never open the modal = No**

* **Given** a Requestor creates a Delivery or Ride request and never opens the Suggested Offer Assistance modal,
* **When** they submit the request,
* **Then** the order record's `suggested_offer_used` value is `false` and displays as **No** in the Admin Panel.

**Scenario 4 — Non-applicable request types are null**

* **Given** a Requestor submits a request that is not Delivery or Ride Sharing,
* **When** the order record is created,
* **Then** `suggested_offer_used` is `null` / blank — the column displays empty for that row.

**Scenario 5 — Historic orders are not backfilled**

* **Given** the feature has shipped,
* **When** an admin opens the Orders report or any order detail view for an order submitted before the feature shipped,
* **Then** `suggested_offer_used` is `null` / blank for that order — no value has been inferred or backfilled.

**Scenario 6 — Admin Panel column visibility and filter**

* **Given** the feature has shipped,
* **When** an admin generates the Orders report,
* **Then** a new column named **Suggested Offer Used** is present and the report can be filtered, sorted, and exported on that column.

**Scenario 7 — Admin Panel order detail visibility**

* **Given** the feature has shipped,
* **When** an admin opens any individual order's detail view,
* **Then** a **Suggested Offer Used: Yes/No** field is visible (or blank for non-applicable orders).

**Scenario 8 — Value is immutable after submission**

* **Given** an order has been submitted with a `suggested_offer_used` value,
* **When** any subsequent change is made to the order (status changes, completion, cancellation, etc.),
* **Then** the `suggested_offer_used` value remains unchanged from what was set at submission.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* `suggested_offer_used = true` **only** when the request was submitted via the Suggested Offer Assistance modal's SUBMIT button. Slider position at submission is irrelevant — anywhere within Low–Generous still counts as Yes.
* The flag applies **only** to Delivery and Ride Sharing requests in this release. All other request types: `null`.
* **No backfill.** Orders submitted before this feature ships remain `null` and are never inferred.
* The flag is set **once, at submission**, and is immutable thereafter.
* The flag must be visible in **both** the Orders report (as a filterable column) **and** the order detail view (as a Yes/No field).

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* The submission path that triggers `true` is specifically the SUBMIT button on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal — that is the only signal needed; do not also try to detect slider movement, time on screen, etc.
* Capture should happen server-side at the request submission API, not client-side only — the API call needs to receive an explicit indicator of which submission path was used.
* If future request types are added to the suggested-pricing flow, the same field should be reused rather than introducing a parallel field per request type.
* Recommend exposing this in any existing analytics or BI export pipeline that already pulls from the Orders table, so downstream reporting picks it up automatically.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Submit a Delivery request via the SUBMIT button on the Suggested Offer Assistance modal — confirm `suggested_offer_used = Yes` in both the Orders report column and the order detail view.
* Submit a Delivery request after tapping BACK out of the modal — confirm `suggested_offer_used = No`.
* Submit a Delivery request without ever opening the modal — confirm `suggested_offer_used = No`.
* Repeat all three above for Ride Sharing.
* Submit a non-Delivery, non-Ride request — confirm `suggested_offer_used` is blank in both views.
* View an order created before this feature shipped — confirm the field is blank (no backfill).
* Generate the Orders report and confirm the new column is present, filterable, sortable, and included in any export.
* Take an order with `Yes` set and run it through status transitions (accepted, completed, cancelled) — confirm the value remains `Yes` throughout.

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* This ticket depends on the existing Suggested Offer Assistance modal being live for Delivery and Ride Sharing. Reference screenshot of the modal is attached to this ticket.
* The Orders report and order detail view in the Admin Panel are assumed to exist already — this ticket adds one column and one field, not a new view.
* This is purely a capture-and-display ticket; no behavioural change to pricing or to the Requestor's experience is in scope.

Summary: AI - Machine Learning Enhancement to Suggested Pricing
Description:
## Goal

Enhance the **suggested-pricing** algorithm (currently a static function of COGS only) to factor in demand/context signals.

**Add:** Day of week · Time of day · Google-recognized holidays · for **"Gopher can purchase from anywhere"** requests, distance from pickup to drop-off.

**Nature:** backend/pricing — **developer-only** (pricing logic fenced from AI edits). This ticket is groomed to a zero-discovery spec.

**▶ Full spec:** `docs/handoff/G40-122-smart-pricing-ml-enhancement.md`

## Current algorithm (the seam)

`controllers/order/create.js` → `get_smart_price` (\~lines 156-186). Takes only `service_cost` (sc):

```
base = 10.0; multiplier tiered by sc (0.10–0.20 for sc≥25; 0 below)
suggested_offer = base + multiplier * sc
```

Only input is COGS. _(Incidental:_ `sc===50` falls through to multiplier 0 — use `>=50`; `sc<25` returns flat $10.)

## Near-term deterministic design (ship before the model)

```
core         = base + multiplier(sc) * sc
demandFactor = dowFactor * todFactor * holidayFactor   // config lookup tables
distanceComp = isShopAnywhere ? perMileRate * miles(pickup,dropoff) : 0
suggested_offer = round(core * demandFactor + distanceComp)
```

* **dow/tod** — tuned lookup tables (weekend/evening higher).
* **holiday** — Google Calendar "US Holidays" (or holidays lib), cached yearly.
* **distance** — Google Maps Distance Matrix (Maps already integrated, RFP Annex §3), pickup→dropoff, shop-anywhere type only.
* **New inputs to** `get_smart_price`: `requested_at` (→ dow/tod), request type/category (→ isShopAnywhere), pickup+dropoff coords (→ miles). Today it only receives `service_cost`.

## ML path (AI-Inclusion epic G40-3)

Log each suggestion (features) with the realized **accepted offer** + time-to-accept (sources: `orders`, `orders_cogs.original_offer/original_cost`; or a new `pricing_suggestions` log). Train sc/dow/tod/holiday/distance/geo/category → accepted-offer; serve behind the same endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Suggestion factors day-of-week, time-of-day, and US holidays (not just COGS).
2. "Purchase-from-anywhere" requests add a pickup→dropoff distance component.
3. Logic centralized in `get_smart_price`; client contract unchanged.
4. Suggestions + accepted offers logged for later model training.

Summary: Gopher Go - Platform Stability Issue
Description:
> 🔧 **DEV-READY HANDOFF — groomed 2026-07-02 (John Newbury).** No prototype build (native-lifecycle behavior); the core logic is already scaffolded + tested. No open questions. Full handoff: `docs/handoff/G40-139-available-tab-instant-refresh.md`.

## 🎯 The real issue (title is vague)

The **Available tab is slow to show new requests** after a push. The feed must refresh **instantly (\~1–2s)** when (a) the app opens via a push notification, (b) it returns to the foreground, or (c) a new-request payload arrives while open — **no** manual pull-to-refresh, **no** full reload/flash, and **no** scroll-position loss.

## 🧩 Core logic already scaffolded + tested (owner)

`G40-Build-Recap.md` → `wave2/g40-139/refreshDecider.js` (+ `useAvailableRefresh.jsx`): _refresh on push-foreground / app-foreground / in-app payload, debounced; hook wires Capacitor lifecycle; preserve scroll._ **Wire the FE to this; don't re-derive.**

## 📱 Developer work (native/FE runtime)

1. Mount `useAvailableRefresh` on the Available tab; drive `refreshDecider` on: **app-foreground-via-push** (iOS AppDelegate/SceneDelegate; Android `onResume`/foreground handler; Capacitor `App` resume + push `pushNotificationReceived`/`ActionPerformed`), **app-foreground-from-background**, and **in-app new-request payload** (foreground push, or a live socket event — confirm the channel is active + triggers the UI update).
2. **Debounce** overlapping triggers to one fetch; do an **incremental** update (no full reload) — preserve scroll, no flash.
3. Replace any polling-interval / tab-focus-only fetch causing the delay.

## 🖼️ Prototype

No build — the static prototype has no push/lifecycle/backend. Visual reference only: the **“Available jobs”** frame in `_prototypes/Go/gopher-go-prototype.html`.

## ✅ Acceptance (from ticket)

Open-via-push → request already visible (no manual refresh); app-open → real-time populate on notification; foreground-no-notification → immediate refetch; visible within **1–2s**; **no UI disruption or scroll loss**; iOS + Android.

---

## 📜 Original ticket (retained)

When a Gopher receives a push for a new available request, the Available tab takes significant time to refresh and show it — in a time-sensitive marketplace, Gophers miss requests. The tab must update immediately on push-open, foreground, or in-app new-request notification. Likely caused by a polling interval / full reload rather than a foreground/notification-triggered fetch. (Full ACs, repro, and QA notes preserved in the handoff doc.)

Summary: Both apps — Block sign-ups that match an admin-deactivated account on 2+ of Name/DOB/Address and route to support
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher trust & safety system protecting the platform from deactivated users returning under new credentials,

## 🎯 I want

to block new sign-ups whose identity matches a previously admin-deactivated user on at least 2 of 3 identity fields (Name, DOB, Address),

## ✅ So that

previously banned users cannot evade the ban simply by using a new Google Voice phone number and a fresh email address.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* The existing duplicate-prevention logic already blocks sign-ups that reuse a known phone number or email — those mechanisms are out of scope for this ticket and continue to operate as today.
* The **evasion pattern this ticket targets**: deactivated users obtain a fresh Google Voice phone number and a new email, then attempt to re-create an account. Phone/email checks miss this because both values are new — but the underlying identity (real name, date of birth, address) is the same.
* This ticket adds an **identity-matching layer** on top of the existing duplicate-prevention logic: at sign-up, compare the new applicant's Name, DOB, and Address against the pool of admin-deactivated accounts. If at least 2 of the 3 fields match a single deactivated account, hard-block the sign-up and route the user to support.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* At sign-up submission on **either app** (Gopher / Gopher Go), the system evaluates the applicant's Name, DOB, and Address against the pool of accounts that an admin has deactivated.
* **Match threshold:** at least **2 of 3** fields must match against the **same** deactivated account (not 2 different fields across 2 different deactivated accounts).
* If the threshold is met:

    * The sign-up is **hard-blocked at submission** — the new account is not created.
    * The applicant is shown a message directing them to **contact support@gophergo.io**.
    * The match event is **logged in the Admin Panel** for support visibility and audit.
    * Only an **admin manually overriding** the block can allow the applicant to proceed.
    
* If the threshold is not met, sign-up continues normally through existing flows.
* Phone number and email are **not** part of this match logic — they continue to be evaluated by the existing duplicate-prevention mechanisms.

---

## 🔍 Matching Rules

| Field | Match precision |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | **Exact** case-insensitive match on first name + last name. No fuzzy / typo tolerance. |
| **DOB** | **Exact** match on YYYY-MM-DD. |
| **Address** | **Full address including unit number** — normalised street, unit, city, state, zip. _Note: this is a defaulted decision — see Open Questions below._ |
| **Matching pool** | Only accounts deactivated by an admin (admin-initiated bans for cause). Self-deleted accounts and inactive auto-deactivations are **not** in the pool. |
| **Threshold** | At least **2 of 3** fields match against the **same** deactivated account. |
| **Persistence** | The match rule applies **forever** — there is no time-based expiry. The block can only be lifted by an admin. |

---

## 💬 User-Facing Experience (draft — confirm copy)

When the threshold is met at sign-up submission, display a blocking message:

* **Title:** Account Cannot Be Created
* **Body:** We're unable to create your account at this time. Please contact our support team at **support@gophergo.io** for assistance.
* **Primary action:** Tap-to-email link that opens the user's mail client with `support@gophergo.io` pre-filled in the To field.

The user must **not** be told _why_ they were blocked or which fields matched. Disclosure here would teach evaders exactly how to bypass the check.

---

## 🛡️ Admin Visibility & Audit

* Every match-and-block event must be recorded in an admin-visible log with the following fields:

    * Timestamp of the sign-up attempt.
    * Applicant's submitted Name, DOB, Address, email, and phone number.
    * The matched **deactivated account ID** and the **specific fields that matched** (e.g., Name + DOB).
    * The applicant's IP address and device identifier where available.
    
* The log must be queryable so support can quickly locate the relevant record when an applicant emails in.
* Admins must have the ability to **manually allow** a previously blocked applicant to proceed — either by clearing the block on the matched deactivated account, or by approving the specific applicant.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Two of three fields match → hard block**

* **Given** an applicant submits sign-up details whose Name, DOB, and Address fields produce a 2-of-3 match against a single admin-deactivated account,
* **When** the sign-up is submitted,
* **Then** the account is not created, the applicant sees the blocking message, and a match event is logged in the Admin Panel.

**Scenario 2 — All three fields match → hard block**

* **Given** an applicant matches a deactivated account on all three of Name, DOB, and Address,
* **When** the sign-up is submitted,
* **Then** the same hard-block behaviour applies as Scenario 1.

**Scenario 3 — Only one field matches → sign-up proceeds**

* **Given** an applicant matches a deactivated account on only one field (e.g., shared household address but different name and DOB),
* **When** the sign-up is submitted,
* **Then** the sign-up proceeds normally through existing flows.

**Scenario 4 — Matches split across two different deactivated accounts → sign-up proceeds**

* **Given** an applicant matches deactivated account A on Name and deactivated account B on Address (1 of 3 against each, not 2 of 3 against any single account),
* **When** the sign-up is submitted,
* **Then** the sign-up proceeds normally — the 2-of-3 threshold must be met against the **same** deactivated account.

**Scenario 5 — Self-deleted accounts do not participate in the match pool**

* **Given** a user who self-deleted their account previously attempts to re-create an account with the same identity,
* **When** the sign-up is submitted,
* **Then** the sign-up proceeds normally — self-deletions are not in the matching pool.

**Scenario 6 — Applicant is not told why they were blocked**

* **Given** the blocking message is shown to the applicant,
* **When** the applicant reads the message,
* **Then** the message does not name which deactivated account, which fields matched, or any other detail that would teach evasion.

**Scenario 7 — Admin can manually override**

* **Given** an applicant has been blocked by this rule and contacted support,
* **When** an admin investigates and decides to allow the applicant,
* **Then** the admin can clear the block and the applicant can complete sign-up.

**Scenario 8 — Audit log is created on every block**

* **Given** any sign-up is blocked by this rule,
* **When** the block fires,
* **Then** the Admin Panel records a match event including timestamp, applicant identifiers, matched deactivated account ID, and which fields matched.

**Scenario 9 — Both apps covered**

* **Given** the feature has shipped,
* **When** an applicant attempts sign-up on either Gopher or Gopher Go,
* **Then** the same matching, blocking, and logging behaviour applies.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* The matching pool consists **only** of accounts that an admin has deactivated for cause. Self-deletions and inactivity-based deactivations are excluded.
* The threshold is **2 of 3 fields against the same deactivated account.** Matches that span multiple deactivated accounts do not aggregate toward the threshold.
* **Name** must match exactly (case-insensitive) on first + last. No fuzzy or typo-tolerant matching.
* **DOB** must match exactly.
* **Address** matching defaults to full address including unit number (see Open Questions).
* Phone number and email are **not** part of this rule. The existing duplicate-prevention logic for those fields continues to operate independently.
* The block is **hard** — only an admin can lift it. There is no automatic appeal or time-based unlock.
* The blocking message must not disclose the reason or matched fields to the applicant.
* The audit log must capture every match event for support and compliance.
* This rule applies to **both** apps (Gopher and Gopher Go).

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* Matching should run **server-side** at the sign-up submission API, never client-side. A client-side check would be trivially bypassable.
* Address normalisation is critical — "123 Main St Apt 4" and "123 Main Street, #4" should match. Use a standard address-normalisation library or service before comparison; do not rely on raw string equality.
* Name normalisation should strip leading/trailing whitespace and lowercase before comparison.
* The matching query should be indexed on the deactivated-account pool to keep sign-up latency acceptable.
* Consider whether a banned user creating an account that matches but does NOT trigger the 2-of-3 threshold (e.g., changes their DOB by one year) should also create a lower-severity audit event for support pattern-recognition. Out of scope for this ticket but worth flagging.
* Recommend deploying behind a feature flag so the block can be toggled off quickly if false-positive rates exceed support capacity.

---

## ⚠️ Open Question Still to Resolve

* **Apartment unit handling.** The current default is to match on the full address **including unit number**. The trade-off:

    * **Including unit (current default):** fewer false positives in apartment buildings and shared housing, but easier to evade by changing the unit number.
    * **Excluding unit (street + city + zip only):** harder to evade, but creates false positives for unrelated residents at the same building / complex.  
      Please confirm or override.
    

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Create a test admin-deactivated account with known Name, DOB, and Address.
* Attempt sign-up with all three matching — expect hard block + audit log + support message.
* Attempt sign-up with two of three matching — expect hard block.
* Attempt sign-up with one of three matching — expect normal sign-up to proceed.
* Attempt sign-up where matches split across two different deactivated accounts — expect normal sign-up to proceed.
* Create a self-deleted account with matching identity and attempt sign-up — expect normal sign-up to proceed.
* Verify the blocking message does not reveal any matched fields or account identifiers.

Summary: Both Accounts - Minimum Age To Sign Up Is 16
Description:
Both apps currently allow users of any age to complete the sign-up flow. A minimum age of 16 must be enforced during account creation. Users who are under 16 must be blocked from creating an account with a clear, friendly message explaining the age requirement.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

platform enforcing minimum age requirements,

## 🎯 I want

to prevent any user under the age of 16 from completing account registration on either app,

## ✅ So that

the platform complies with its minimum age policy and underage users cannot access the marketplace.

## 💡 Context / Background

* The sign-up flow currently collects a date of birth but does not enforce a minimum age gate — users of any age can complete registration.
* The minimum age to create an account on either app is 16.
* When a user enters a date of birth that indicates they are under 16, account creation must be blocked immediately with a clear message.
* This applies to both the Gopher App (Requestor) and Gopher Go (Gopher).

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Gopher App or Gopher Go.
2. Begin the sign-up flow.
3. Enter a date of birth that results in an age under 16.
4. Observe that the sign-up flow continues and the account is created without any age restriction error.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* Users under 16 can complete the sign-up flow and create an account without any restriction
* No age validation or minimum age gate is enforced at sign-up

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* When a user enters a date of birth indicating they are under 16, account creation is blocked
* A clear, friendly message is displayed explaining that users must be at least 16 to create an account
* The user cannot proceed past the date of birth step if they are under 16

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – User under 16 is blocked from signing up

* **Given** a user enters a date of birth that makes them under 16 years old
* **When** they attempt to proceed past the date of birth step
* **Then** account creation is blocked and a message is displayed: "You must be at least 16 years old to create an account."
* **And** the user cannot continue the sign-up flow

### Scenario 2 – User exactly 16 can sign up

* **Given** a user enters a date of birth that makes them exactly 16 years old
* **When** they proceed past the date of birth step
* **Then** the sign-up flow continues normally

### Scenario 3 – User 17 or older can sign up

* **Given** a user enters a date of birth that makes them 17 or older
* **When** they proceed past the date of birth step
* **Then** the sign-up flow continues normally with no age-related block

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* The minimum age to create an account on either app is 16.
* Age validation must be enforced on the backend as well as the frontend — frontend-only validation is not sufficient.
* Age is calculated based on the user’s date of birth relative to today’s date — a user whose 16th birthday is today is eligible.
* This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Confirm that date of birth is already collected during sign-up — if not, it must be added as a required field.
* Age validation must be performed on the backend at the time the profile data is submitted, not just on the frontend, to prevent bypass.
* Existing accounts created by users under 16 should be flagged for admin review — confirm with the team whether any remediation of existing under-age accounts is required.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Enter a DOB that makes the user 15 years old — confirm sign-up is blocked with the correct message.
* Enter a DOB that makes the user exactly 16 today — confirm sign-up proceeds.
* Enter a DOB that makes the user 17 or older — confirm sign-up proceeds normally.
* Attempt to bypass the frontend validation via the API with an underage DOB — confirm the backend also rejects the request.
* Test on both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Favorite Gopher (MY Gopher) Recommendation View In Inbox Issue
Description:
When a Requestor receives a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message, three issues are present: the View Profile link for recommended Gophers does not open the profile popup modal as intended, the SMS sent to the referred party is missing app download links, and on Android the inbox message cannot be scrolled to reveal all recommended Gophers at the bottom of the list.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Requestor who has received a MY Gopher recommendation in their inbox,

## 🎯 I want

to be able to view each recommended Gopher’s profile, receive a working SMS with app links, and scroll to see all recommendations,

## ✅ So that

I can fully evaluate each recommended Gopher and the referral experience works end-to-end.

## 💡 Context / Background

* When a Gopher App user uses Refer App → Recommend MY Gopher, the recipient receives an inbox message with a list of one or more recommended Gophers.
* Each recommended Gopher is displayed with their profile picture and a View Profile label to the left.
* Tapping anywhere from the profile picture to the View Profile text should open the standard Gopher profile popup modal — the same format used when viewing bids, interested Gophers, and counter offers.
* The referred party also receives an SMS notification about the recommendation. This SMS is missing the app download links.
* On Android devices, the inbox message list cannot be scrolled, cutting off any Gophers at the bottom of the recommendation list.

## ⚠️ Issue Breakdown

### Bug 1 – View Profile Link Not Functioning

* Tapping the recommended Gopher’s profile picture or the View Profile text in the inbox message does not open the profile popup modal
* The tappable area must span from the profile picture through to the View Profile label
* The profile popup modal that opens must match the format used for viewing bids, interested Gophers, and counter offers

### Bug 2 – SMS Missing App Download Links

* The SMS sent to the referred party when a MY Gopher recommendation is made does not include links to download the apps
* The SMS must include the following deep links:

* **Gopher App (Requestor):** https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/requester
* **Gopher Go:** https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/go

### Bug 3 – Android Scroll Issue (Bottom Gopher Not Visible)

* On Android, the inbox message view containing recommended Gophers cannot be scrolled
* When two or more Gophers are recommended, the bottom Gopher is cut off and inaccessible
* The recommended Gopher list must be scrollable on Android so all recommendations are accessible

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

### Bug 1 – View Profile

1. Receive a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message with at least one recommended Gopher.
2. Open the inbox message.
3. Tap the recommended Gopher’s profile picture or the View Profile text.
4. Observe that the profile popup modal does not open.

### Bug 2 – SMS App Links

1. Have a Gopher App user send a MY Gopher recommendation via Refer App.
2. Check the SMS received by the referred party.
3. Observe that no app download links are included.

### Bug 3 – Android Scroll

1. On an Android device, open a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message with two or more recommended Gophers.
2. Attempt to scroll down to see the bottom recommended Gopher.
3. Observe the list does not scroll and the bottom Gopher is cut off.

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Tapping a recommended Gopher opens the profile popup modal

* **Given** a Requestor has opened a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message
* **When** they tap the recommended Gopher’s profile picture or the View Profile text
* **Then** the Gopher’s profile popup modal opens in the standard format used for bids, interested Gophers, and counter offers

### Scenario 2 – Referral SMS includes app download links

* **Given** a MY Gopher recommendation has been sent to a referred party
* **When** the referred party receives the SMS
* **Then** the SMS contains links to both the Gopher App (https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/requester) and Gopher Go (https://api.gophergo.io/api/v1/app/go)

### Scenario 3 – Android inbox message is scrollable

* **Given** an Android user opens a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message with multiple recommended Gophers
* **When** they scroll down in the inbox message
* **Then** all recommended Gophers are visible and accessible

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* The tappable area on each recommended Gopher must span from the profile picture to the View Profile text.
* The profile modal opened from the recommendation must match the exact format used elsewhere in the app for Gopher profile views.
* The referral SMS must always include both app download links.
* The recommendation list in the inbox message must be scrollable on both iOS and Android regardless of the number of Gophers listed.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Bug 1: Confirm whether the View Profile tap target is missing an onPress handler or whether the profile modal component is not being rendered in the inbox context.
* Bug 2: Update the SMS template for MY Gopher referrals to include both app deep links.
* Bug 3: The Android scroll issue is likely caused by a non-scrollable container wrapping the recommended Gopher list — ensure the list is wrapped in a ScrollView or FlatList with appropriate height constraints.
* Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=105-15465

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Open a MY Gopher recommendation inbox message and tap a recommended Gopher’s profile picture — confirm the profile modal opens.
* Tap the View Profile text — confirm the profile modal opens.
* Confirm the profile modal matches the standard format used for bids and interested Gophers.
* Send a MY Gopher recommendation and check the referred party’s SMS — confirm both app links are present and tappable.
* On Android, open a recommendation message with 2+ Gophers — confirm the list scrolls and all Gophers are accessible.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher Go - Available Request View - Remove Customer Apt #
Description:
The Gopher Go Available tab is exposing the customer’s apartment or unit number to Gophers before a request has been accepted. The platform already hides the physical street address numbers prior to acceptance for privacy. The apartment/unit number must follow the same rule and be hidden until the request is accepted. This applies to all request types.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

platform protecting Requestor privacy,

## 🎯 I want

the customer’s apartment or unit number to be hidden from Gophers on the Available tab until they have accepted the request,

## ✅ So that

the Requestor’s specific unit details are not exposed to Gophers who have not been entrusted with fulfilling their request.

## 💡 Context / Background

* The platform already hides the physical street address numbers (e.g. house number or building number) from Gophers on the Available tab until a request is accepted.
* The apartment or unit number is a more specific piece of identifying information and must be subject to the same privacy restriction.
* Currently, the apartment/unit number is visible to all Gophers browsing available requests before acceptance.
* This applies to all request types across Gopher Go.

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Log in to Gopher Go as a Gopher.
2. Navigate to the Available tab.
3. Open any available request where the Requestor has entered an apartment or unit number.
4. Observe that the apartment/unit number is visible before acceptance.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* The customer’s apartment or unit number is visible to all Gophers on the Available tab before a request is accepted
* The street address numbers are already correctly hidden, but the unit/apt number is not

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* The apartment or unit number is hidden from Gophers on the Available tab before acceptance
* Once a Gopher accepts the request, the full address including the apartment/unit number is revealed
* This behavior is consistent across all request types

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Apt/unit number is hidden before acceptance

* **Given** a Gopher is browsing available requests
* **When** they view a request where the Requestor has entered an apartment or unit number
* **Then** the apartment or unit number is not visible

### Scenario 2 – Full address including apt/unit is revealed after acceptance

* **Given** a Gopher has accepted a request
* **When** they view the request details
* **Then** the full address including the apartment or unit number is displayed

### Scenario 3 – Applies to all request types

* **Given** any request type (Delivery, Need A Ride, Service, etc.) where an apt/unit number is entered
* **When** a Gopher views the request before accepting
* **Then** the apt/unit number is hidden

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* The apartment or unit number must be treated as private address information and hidden from Gophers until a request is accepted.
* This rule applies consistently to all request types and all address fields — street number and unit/apt number are both hidden pre-acceptance.
* The full address must be revealed immediately upon request acceptance.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Identify where the address is being constructed for display on the Available tab and confirm the unit/apt field is being excluded from the pre-acceptance masked address string.
* The masking logic that already hides the street number should be extended to also strip the apartment or unit number from the pre-acceptance address display.
* Confirm the full unmasked address (including unit/apt) is correctly surfaced once the request is accepted.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Create a request with an apartment or unit number and view it as a Gopher on the Available tab before accepting — confirm the apt/unit number is not visible.
* Accept the request and confirm the full address including the apt/unit number is now visible.
* Test across multiple request types — Delivery, Need A Ride, Service — to confirm consistent behavior.
* Confirm the street address number is also still hidden before acceptance (regression check).
* Test on both iOS and Android.

## Goal

On the Gopher's **active request** screen, tapping **Pick-Up** or **Destination** opens a modal with **3 navigation options** — Google Maps (already integrated), Apple Maps, Waze — with a **set-default-platform** option, an **auto-prompt** when items are picked up, and a **purchase-from-anywhere countdown timer**.

Summary: User Story - Allow Dynamic Updating of Gopher Fee, Instant Transfer Fee and Age-Restricted Fee
Description:
## Goal

Fees on Gopher requests must be **dynamic and editable via the admin portal** — currently hard-coded in `gopher-backend-api/constants/index.js`. Three fees: **Gopher Fee**, **Instant Transfer Fee**, **Age-Restricted Fee**. DB, backend, and admin panel all need updating.

**▶ Full handoff:** `docs/handoff/G40-176-dynamic-fees.md`

## ✅ Already coded — "Pricing Control" tool in the HQ Dashboard

**Where:** `Documentation/Dashboard/app_part4.js` → `VIEWS.pricing` (Pricing Control tab, `app_part1.js:169`, **OWNER**-gated). Renders in `output/Gopher_HQ_Dashboard.html`.

**Model** (`seedPricing()`, app_part4.js:284) — single source of truth seeded from the canonical pricing sheet:

```
PRICING = {
  gopherFee: { <category>: { request, connectStd, connectBiz } },  // 8 cats × 3 surfaces
  ageFee:    { request:1.99, connectStd:2.99, connectBiz:2.99 },   // Age-Restricted Fee
  instantTransfer: 0.08,                                           // Instant Transfer Fee
  deal: { serviceWaivesAll, boostPct }, _publishedAt }
```

All three fees are **editable today**: per-category×surface $ inputs, age-restricted row, instant-transfer % (`#px-it`).

**Working now:** editable schedule table · owner gate (`ROLE==='owner'`) · live **audit log** (`PRICING_AUDIT`/`logChange`) · live **parity check** vs backend + Connect client (`parityVs()`; CI script `pricing_parity_check.py`) · **backend patch generator** (`genBackendPatch()`, app_part4.js:398 — emits `FEE_SCHEDULES` + `INSTANT_TRANSFER_RATE` for `constants/index.js`) · Export/Import config. **Persistence today = localStorage** (prototype seam — not yet reaching the real DB/BE).

## 🔧 To build — connect the tool to DB / BE / FE

1. **DB:** `fee_schedules` table storing the full PRICING model (per surface×category gopher fee, ageFee/surface, instantTransfer, deal, published_at) + `fee_schedule_audit` table mirroring `PRICING_AUDIT`.
2. **Backend:** replace hard-coded fees in `constants/index.js` with a **cached DB read** (shape = `genBackendPatch()` output). Update consumers: `create.js` (`application_fee` by category/surface, `age_restricted_fee`), `lib/payment.stripe.js` (instant-transfer rate). Add owner-only `PUT/GET /admin/pricing`.
3. **Dashboard:** point `seedPricing()`/`persistPricing()` at `GET/PUT /admin/pricing` instead of localStorage — everything else stays.
4. **Client apps (FE):** consumer app + `gopher-connect.html` currently hard-code schedules (`GOPHER_FEE`/`AGE_FEE`/business) — point them at `GET /pricing?surface=…`; keep `pricing_parity_check.py` as the CI guard.

_Bonus:_ the backend ships no Connect schedule today, so Connect age-restricted orders fall back to $1.99 instead of $2.99 — the surface-aware DB shape fixes that.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Owner edits Gopher / Age-Restricted / Instant-Transfer fees in the dashboard — **done** (Pricing Control).
2. Edits persist to the **DB** via an owner-only admin API — _to build_.
3. Backend charges from the **DB-driven** schedule, not `constants/index.js` — _to build_.
4. Client apps display fees consistent with the DB (parity green) — _to build_.
5. Every change is audit-logged — **done** in-tool; persist server-side — _to build_.
