Summary: Gopher App - Available Gophers Calculation Update
Description:
When a user submits an address while creating a request, the system must calculate and display an accurate count of eligible Gophers available for that request. The calculation must apply a strict set of qualification criteria and trigger a low-availability warning modal if fewer than 20 eligible Gophers are found.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Requestor entering details for a new request,

## 🎯 I want

the app to show an accurate count of Gophers who are genuinely available and qualified for my request,

## ✅ So that

I have a realistic expectation of how quickly my request can be fulfilled and am warned if availability is low in my area.

## 💡 Context / Background

* The available Gopher headcount displayed during request creation is currently not filtered accurately enough.
* It may include Gophers who are unverified, inactive, out of range, or whose work settings do not match the request category.
* The calculation must be triggered when the Requestor submits their pick-up and/or drop-off address during request entry.
* If the qualified Gopher count falls below 20, a low-availability modal must be shown to the Requestor.

## 📍 Eligible Gopher Criteria

A Gopher is only counted as available if ALL of the following conditions are met:

* **Stripe Payout Account Verified** — only Gophers with a verified Stripe payout account are eligible
* **Within 15 Miles** — the Gopher’s GPS location or physical profile address must be within 15 miles of the pick-up and/or drop-off address
* **Work Settings & Radius Match** — the Gopher’s work settings and service radius must match the category being requested
* **Active Within Last 6 Months** — the Gopher must have logged in within the last 6 months

## ❌ Current Behavior

* The available Gopher count does not apply all required qualification filters
* Unverified, inactive, out-of-range, or category-mismatched Gophers may be included in the count
* The displayed headcount may be inflated and does not reflect genuine availability
* No low-availability warning is triggered when eligible Gophers are scarce

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* When a Requestor submits an address during request creation, the system recalculates the eligible Gopher count using all four qualification criteria
* Only Gophers meeting all criteria are counted
* The accurate eligible headcount is displayed to the Requestor
* If fewer than 20 eligible Gophers are found, a low-availability warning modal is displayed to the Requestor

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Eligible count is calculated on address submission

* **Given** a Requestor submits a pick-up or drop-off address during request creation
* **When** the address is submitted
* **Then** the system recalculates the eligible Gopher count applying all four qualification criteria
* **And** the accurate count is displayed to the Requestor

### Scenario 2 – Unqualified Gophers are excluded from the count

* **Given** Gophers exist who are unverified, inactive, out of range, or whose work settings do not match the category
* **When** the eligible count is calculated
* **Then** those Gophers are excluded from the count

### Scenario 3 – Low-availability modal triggers when fewer than 20 eligible Gophers are found

* **Given** the eligible Gopher count for the request is fewer than 20
* **When** the count is calculated
* **Then** the low-availability warning modal is displayed to the Requestor

### Scenario 4 – No modal when 20 or more eligible Gophers are available

* **Given** the eligible Gopher count is 20 or more
* **When** the count is calculated
* **Then** no low-availability modal is shown and the Requestor proceeds normally

### Scenario 5 – Count updates when address changes

* **Given** a Requestor updates their pick-up or drop-off address after an initial calculation
* **When** the new address is submitted
* **Then** the eligible Gopher count is recalculated and updated accordingly

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* All four eligibility criteria must be applied simultaneously — a Gopher must meet every condition to be counted.
* Location is determined using the Gopher’s GPS location where available, falling back to their physical profile address.
* The 15-mile proximity check applies to the pick-up and/or drop-off address submitted by the Requestor.
* Work settings and service radius must match the specific category being requested, not just general availability.
* A Gopher who has not logged in within the last 6 months is considered inactive and must be excluded.
* The low-availability modal must trigger when the eligible count is fewer than 20, regardless of the total Gopher count in the system.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Calculation must be triggered on address submission during request creation, not on page load.
* GPS location data for Gophers must be accessible at calculation time — confirm availability and fallback logic with the backend team.
* Stripe verification status must be queryable as part of the eligibility filter.
* Gopher work settings and service radius data must be structured to support category-level filtering.
* Reference Figma for the low-availability modal design: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=15-3913

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Test with an address that has 20 or more eligible Gophers — confirm accurate count is displayed and no modal appears.
* Test with an address that has fewer than 20 eligible Gophers — confirm the low-availability modal is triggered.
* Verify unverified Gophers (no Stripe payout account) are excluded from the count.
* Verify Gophers outside the 15-mile radius are excluded.
* Verify Gophers whose work settings or service radius do not match the request category are excluded.
* Verify Gophers who have not logged in within the last 6 months are excluded.
* Test updating the address after an initial calculation — confirm the count recalculates correctly.
* Test across multiple request categories to ensure work settings filtering applies correctly per category.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Both apps — Require OTP to change profile email, then notify old + new address with support escalation path
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

User of either app (Gopher / Gopher Go) updating the email address on my profile,

## 🎯 I want

the change to be OTP-verified and confirmed by notification emails sent to both my old and new address,

## ✅ So that

my email cannot be silently changed by anyone other than me, and if a change ever does happen without my knowledge, I have an immediate notification at my existing address with a clear path to recover the account.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* Email is the primary identifier for an account and the channel through which password resets and other security-critical messages flow. An attacker who silently changes the email locks the legitimate owner out.
* The existing **standard email OTP** mechanism (already used elsewhere in the apps) is reused here — no new OTP component is built.
* The dual-notification pattern (old + new address) is the standard industry approach to protect against account takeover: even if an attacker controls a session, the legitimate owner will see the notification at their existing address and can escalate immediately.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

### Email change flow

1. User initiates an email change from **My Profile** by entering a new email address.
2. **Pre-OTP validation:**

    * If the new email is the **same** as the current email on file, reject with **"No change detected"** and do not send an OTP.
    * If the new email is **already in use on another account**, reject with **"This email address is not available"** and do not send an OTP.
    * If the new email is **invalid format**, reject with a standard format-validation message and do not send an OTP.
    
3. **OTP send:** The system sends an OTP via the existing standard OTP flow to the **NEW email address only**.
4. **OTP entry:** The user enters the OTP in the app.

    * OTP retry limits, expiry, and resend behaviour follow the existing standard OTP rules — no bespoke rules apply on this surface.
    
5. **On successful OTP entry:**

    * The email on the user's account is updated to the new address.
    * **Two confirmation emails** are sent:
    
        * One to the **OLD** address.
        * One to the **NEW** address.
        
    * Both use the **standard email template** for the respective app (Gopher / Gopher Go).
    * The event is **logged in the Admin Panel audit trail**.
    
6. **On OTP failure** (exhausted attempts or expired):

    * The email is not changed.
    * The user is returned to the email-change entry point.
    * The failed attempt is logged in the Admin Panel audit trail.
    

---

## 📧 Confirmation Email Content (draft — confirm against existing template style)

Both confirmation emails use the standard template for the respective app and contain:

* **Subject:** Your email address was changed
* **Body:**

Hi \[First Name\],

The email address on your Gopher account was just changed.

* **From:** \[old email address\]
* **To:** \[new email address\]
* **When:** \[timestamp in user's local timezone\]
* **Where:** \[device + approximate location, e.g., "iPhone, Raleigh, NC"\]

If you made this change, no further action is needed.

**If this wasn't you, please contact support@gophergo.io as soon as possible.**

Thanks,

_— The Gopher Team_

---

## 📊 Notification Content Rules

* Include: timestamp (local timezone), device, approximate location (city / region level only).
* Do **not** include: IP address (not user-friendly and adds noise without value).
* Do **not** include: a one-click reversal link in this release — the ticket specifies the support email as the recovery path. If a self-serve revert link is added in future, it would be a separate ticket.
* The body must be identical in content for both the old and new address sends (single source of truth).

---

## 🛡️ Admin Visibility & Audit

Log every email-change event in the Admin Panel with the following fields:

* Timestamp of the attempt.
* Account ID.
* Old email and new email.
* Event type: **Success**, **OTP failure (exhausted/expired)**, or **Duplicate-collision attempt**.
* Device identifier and approximate location.

The log enables security pattern review and gives support an immediate record when a user emails in about an unauthorised change.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Happy path: OTP succeeds, email updates, both addresses notified**

* **Given** a signed-in user enters a valid new email different from their current one and not in use on any other account,
* **When** they submit the change and enter the correct OTP delivered to the new email,
* **Then** the account's email is updated to the new address, a confirmation email is sent to both the old and new addresses, and the change is logged in the Admin Panel.

**Scenario 2 — OTP sent to NEW email only (not OLD)**

* **Given** a user has initiated an email change,
* **When** the OTP is dispatched,
* **Then** it is sent only to the new email address — the old address is not used for OTP.

**Scenario 3 — Same-as-current rejected before OTP**

* **Given** a user enters their current email as the "new" email,
* **When** they submit,
* **Then** the request is rejected with "No change detected" and no OTP is sent.

**Scenario 4 — Duplicate collision rejected before OTP**

* **Given** a user enters a new email that is already in use on another account,
* **When** they submit,
* **Then** the request is rejected with "This email address is not available," no OTP is sent, and the attempt is logged.

**Scenario 5 — Invalid format rejected before OTP**

* **Given** a user enters an email in an invalid format,
* **When** they submit,
* **Then** standard format validation rejects the input and no OTP is sent.

**Scenario 6 — OTP failure does not change the email**

* **Given** a user has been sent an OTP for an email change,
* **When** the user fails OTP entry per existing standard OTP rules (attempts exhausted or expired),
* **Then** the account email remains unchanged, no confirmation emails are sent, and the failed attempt is logged.

**Scenario 7 — Old-address notification supports the "wasn't me" path**

* **Given** a user receives a confirmation email at their old address,
* **When** the user reads the email,
* **Then** the body clearly directs them to email support@gophergo.io if the change was not initiated by them.

**Scenario 8 — Notification contains timestamp + device + location**

* **Given** the confirmation emails are dispatched,
* **When** a user reads either confirmation,
* **Then** the email contains the timestamp (in local time), device identifier, and approximate city/region of the change.

**Scenario 9 — Standard template for the respective app**

* **Given** the change happens on Gopher,
* **When** the confirmation emails are dispatched,
* **Then** they use the Gopher standard email template. The same rule applies for Gopher Go using the Gopher Go template.

**Scenario 10 — Abandoned mid-flow**

* **Given** a user starts an email change and never enters the OTP,
* **When** the OTP expires per existing OTP rules,
* **Then** the email on the account remains the original address — nothing partial is persisted.

**Scenario 11 — Both apps covered**

* **Given** the feature has shipped,
* **When** a user changes their email on either Gopher or Gopher Go,
* **Then** the same OTP, dual-notification, and audit behaviour applies.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* The new email address must pass three pre-OTP checks (different from current, not in use elsewhere, valid format) before any OTP is sent.
* The OTP is sent to the **NEW** email address only — verifying the user controls the destination mailbox.
* OTP retry limits, expiry, and resend behaviour are inherited from the existing standard OTP mechanism — no bespoke rules.
* The email on file is updated **only** after successful OTP entry. No partial state is persisted on abandonment or OTP failure.
* On success, confirmation emails go to **both** the old and new addresses, using the **standard email template** for the respective app.
* The confirmation email includes timestamp, device, and approximate location.
* The confirmation email **does not** include a one-click revert link in this release — support@gophergo.io is the only recovery path.
* Every email-change event (success, OTP failure, duplicate collision) is logged in the Admin Panel audit trail.
* This applies to **both** apps (Gopher and Gopher Go).

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* All checks must run server-side at the email-change API. Client-side validation alone is bypassable.
* The pre-OTP duplicate-email check must run **before** sending the OTP. Sending an OTP first and rejecting after on collision both wastes a delivery and leaks account-existence information via delivery timing.
* The two confirmation emails should be dispatched in parallel from the same job/transaction so neither can succeed without the other.
* The audit log entry should be written in the same transaction as the email update to guarantee record integrity.
* Reuse the existing standard OTP flow and standard email templates wherever they live in the codebase — do not introduce a new OTP service or template variant for this surface.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Initiate an email change with a valid new email — confirm OTP arrives at the new address only.
* Enter the OTP correctly — confirm the email updates, both old and new addresses receive confirmation emails, and the event is in the Admin Panel audit log.
* Repeat with an invalid OTP / expired OTP — confirm the email does not change and the failure is logged.
* Submit the current email as the "new" email — confirm "No change detected" with no OTP sent.
* Submit an email that is in use on another account — confirm rejection with no OTP sent and a logged event.
* Submit an invalid-format email — confirm rejection with no OTP sent.
* Abandon the flow after submitting the new email but before entering the OTP — confirm the account email is unchanged.
* Verify the confirmation email body contains the From / To, timestamp, device, and approximate location.
* Verify the "if this wasn't you" line directs the user to support@gophergo.io.
* Run on both apps (Gopher and Gopher Go) and both iOS and Android.

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Depends on the existing standard email OTP mechanism being usable for this flow.
* Depends on the existing standard email templates for Gopher and Gopher Go.
* Depends on the device + approximate-location signal being available at the email-change API. If only one of those is reliably captured today, it can ship with what's available and the rest added later.
* Out of scope for this ticket: a self-serve "Revert this change" one-click link in the old-address notification. If desired in future, that would be a separate ticket given the additional flow (token issuance, expiry, single-use enforcement) it requires.

Summary: Active Admin - Orders - Allow Admin To Update A Request
Description:
In the Orders tab, an admin can perform any/all functions for a **live** request (advance to in-progress, mark items picked up, mark delivered, etc.). Every admin action stamps the order log/timestamp as **"Updated by admin."**

_Surface: build into the **Gopher HQ Dashboard** order page — Active Admin is being replaced. Groomed dev-ready; full spec in_ `docs/handoff/G40-189-admin-update-live-request.md`.

---

## Current state (verified, June-2026 backend export `e9bf57a3`)

* **Gopher-side lifecycle transitions exist but are scoped to the assigned gopher.** `controllers/order/update.js` advances `aasm_state` (assigned → in_progress → picked_up/purchased → delivered) under `where: { id, gopher_id: decoded.id }`, each writing an `order_logs` row.
* **Admin API exists and is auth-gated** (`routes/admin.routes.js`, `verify_auth` requires JWT `userType==='ADMIN'`), but `controllers/admin/orders.js` can only **cancel** (`cancelOrder`, writes `aasm_state='cancelled'` + `order_logs`) or delete — **no** endpoints to advance a live request.
* `order_logs` has no actor column (`models/order_logs.model.js`) — nothing records that a change came from an admin, so "Updated by admin" has nowhere structured to live.
* **Dashboard order page is read-only** (`app_part4.js` → `renderOrderPage`, `VIEWS.order`): it already renders a "Timing & status" section + Order log (with `Updated at` earmarked) — the exact host slots — but has no action controls.

**Conclusion:** order-detail surface exists both ends; the interactive admin override is **net-new**.

## What to build

1. **DB** — add `updated_by INTEGER` + `source VARCHAR` to `order_logs`; backfill existing rows to `source='gopher'`.
2. **Backend** — in `controllers/admin/orders.js`, add admin-authed lifecycle endpoints (`PATCH /orders/:id/in-progress|picked-up|delivered`, optional generic status) mirroring `update.js` transitions but **without** the `gopher_id` guard; validate legal transitions; write an `order_logs` row stamped `source:'admin', updated_by:req.user.userId`, null geo; fire the same single-recipient status notifications. Mirror `cancelOrder` for structure.
3. **Dashboard** — owner-gated action buttons in the order page's "Timing & status" card for legal next transitions; render admin-sourced log rows with an **"Updated by admin"** badge.
4. **Audit** — the stamped `order_logs` row (who/what/when) is the audit trail; gate strictly to owner/admin.

## Acceptance criteria

* Owner/admin can advance a live order through its legal lifecycle from the dashboard without being the assigned gopher.
* Each action persists the new `aasm_state` + an `order_logs` entry with `source='admin'`, `updated_by=<admin id>`, no gopher GPS.
* The order log renders those entries with an "Updated by admin" label at the correct timestamp.
* Requester/gopher still receive normal status notifications (single-recipient, unchanged).
* Illegal transitions rejected with a clear error; controls hidden from non-admin roles.

Summary: Gopher Go - Completed Request - Age-Restricted Protocol & No Show Feature Used - Payout Delay
Description:
When a Gopher completes an age-restricted request, a structured verification flow must be followed before payout is released. The flow branches based on whether the recipient has TrustShield and whether the customer is present. If the Requestor is a no-show after a 10-minute timer, the payout is paused for 24 hours and the order enters a Confirmation Pending state until resolved by auto-completion or admin action. Additional no-show safeguards require GPS proximity verification, Requestor timer acknowledgment, and a fraud alert on no-show submission. This ticket incorporates all requirements from G40-267.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher completing an age-restricted request,

## 🎯 I want

a clear, structured verification flow that confirms the recipient’s identity before my payout is released,

## ✅ So that

age-restricted deliveries are completed compliantly, fraudulent payouts are prevented, and I am fairly compensated even in no-show situations.

## 💡 Context / Background

* Age-restricted requests require identity verification before a Gopher can complete the order and receive payout.
* The verification flow branches based on whether the recipient has TrustShield (pre-verified identity) or requires on-site ID capture.
* If the recipient is not present, the Gopher triggers a 10-minute wait timer before being able to log a no-show.
* To prevent fraudulent no-show submissions, three additional safeguards apply when a Gopher attempts to submit a Requestor No Show: GPS proximity to the drop-off location must be checked, the Requestor must have acknowledged the timer, and a fraud alert must be triggered on submission.
* The admin team must be notified by email whenever a no-show payout hold is triggered so they can monitor frequency and enforce best practices.
* Admins can manually complete a Confirmation Pending order to expedite payout if needed.

## 🔀 Complete Flow

### Step 1 – Gopher Marks Request Completed

* Gopher taps Update to Completed
* A popup modal is displayed
* If Continue is tapped: GPS location and timestamp are logged in the admin panel
* If "Do Not Show Me Again" was previously selected: tapping Update – Completed automatically triggers the GPS/timestamp log without the popup

### Step 2A – TrustShield Path (Recipient is Pre-Verified)

* The TrustShield verification screen is displayed
* Gopher taps ID and Identity Confirmed
* Gopher is taken to the ratings screen
* Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11580

### Step 2B – No TrustShield Path (On-Site ID Capture Required)

* The active camera screen is displayed for ID capture
* Gopher captures the recipient’s ID
* Gopher taps ID and Identity Confirmed
* Gopher is taken to the ratings screen
* Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11713

### Step 2C – Customer Not Present Path

* Gopher taps Set Timer – Customer Not Present
* A 10-minute countdown timer begins
* Requestor receives a banner notification and text message alerting them the Gopher is waiting — the Requestor must acknowledge this notification
* Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11657

### Step 3 – After 10-Minute Timer Expires

* Gopher is shown two options: Confirm ID and Identity or Requestor No Show
* If Confirm ID and Identity is tapped: flow proceeds to the ratings screen as normal
* If Requestor No Show is tapped, three checks are performed:

* **GPS proximity check** — the system checks whether the Gopher’s current location is within 50 feet (\~15 meters) of the drop-off location’s lat/long. This check is non-blocking — the Gopher can still proceed. However, if the Gopher is outside the 50-foot radius, a warning notification is shown: "You appear to be outside the expected drop-off location. Submitting a no-show from this location will trigger a fraud alert and may affect your payout speed if a dispute arises." The Gopher must confirm to proceed.
* **Requestor acknowledgment check** — the Requestor must have acknowledged the timer notification before the No Show can be submitted. If the Requestor has not acknowledged the timer, the Gopher is shown a message indicating the Requestor has not yet confirmed receipt of the wait notification.
* **Fraud alert trigger** — when a Requestor No Show is submitted, a fraud alert notification is automatically triggered and flagged in the admin panel for review, regardless of GPS proximity.

* Once all checks are passed or acknowledged, payout is paused for 24 hours and the order enters Confirmation Pending status
* Figma reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=24-11685

### Step 4 – Confirmation Pending Resolution

* The order remains in Confirmation Pending status for up to 24 hours
* After 24 hours with no action, the order auto-completes and payout is released
* An admin can manually complete the order in the admin panel at any time to expedite the payout
* An automated notification email is sent to admin@gophergo.io when a no-show payout hold is triggered

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – GPS and timestamp are logged on completion

* **Given** a Gopher taps Completed on an age-restricted request
* **When** Continue is tapped on the popup (or Do Not Show Me Again was previously selected)
* **Then** the Gopher’s GPS location and timestamp are logged in the admin panel

### Scenario 2 – TrustShield path completes to ratings screen

* **Given** the recipient has TrustShield
* **When** the Gopher taps ID and Identity Confirmed
* **Then** the Gopher is taken to the ratings screen and payout is released

### Scenario 3 – No TrustShield path requires ID capture before completion

* **Given** the recipient does not have TrustShield
* **When** the Gopher reaches the completion step
* **Then** the active camera screen is displayed for ID capture
* **And** once ID and Identity Confirmed is tapped, the Gopher proceeds to the ratings screen

### Scenario 4 – Customer Not Present triggers 10-minute timer and Requestor notification

* **Given** the recipient is not present when the Gopher arrives
* **When** the Gopher taps Set Timer – Customer Not Present
* **Then** a 10-minute countdown timer begins and the Requestor receives a banner notification and text message requiring acknowledgment

### Scenario 5 – Gopher within 50 feet can submit No Show without warning

* **Given** the 10-minute timer has expired and the Gopher’s GPS is within 50 feet of the drop-off location
* **When** the Gopher taps Requestor No Show
* **Then** no location warning is shown and the no-show submission proceeds

### Scenario 6 – Gopher outside 50 feet receives a warning before submitting No Show

* **Given** the 10-minute timer has expired and the Gopher’s GPS is more than 50 feet from the drop-off location
* **When** the Gopher taps Requestor No Show
* **Then** a warning is shown: "You appear to be outside the expected drop-off location. Submitting a no-show from this location will trigger a fraud alert and may affect your payout speed if a dispute arises."
* **And** the Gopher must confirm to proceed
* **And** the no-show can still be submitted after confirmation

### Scenario 7 – Requestor No Show triggers fraud alert

* **Given** a Gopher submits a Requestor No Show
* **When** the no-show is confirmed
* **Then** a fraud alert is automatically triggered and flagged in the admin panel for review

### Scenario 8 – Requestor No Show triggers 24-hour payout hold

* **Given** the Gopher has confirmed the no-show submission
* **When** the no-show is processed
* **Then** the payout is paused for 24 hours, the order enters Confirmation Pending status, and an automated email is sent to admin@gophergo.io

### Scenario 9 – Confirmation Pending auto-completes after 24 hours

* **Given** an order is in Confirmation Pending status
* **When** 24 hours pass with no admin action
* **Then** the order auto-completes and the payout is released

### Scenario 10 – Admin can manually complete a Confirmation Pending order

* **Given** an order is in Confirmation Pending status
* **When** an admin manually marks the order as complete
* **Then** the order completes immediately and the payout is released ahead of the 24-hour window

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* Identity verification is mandatory for all age-restricted request completions — payout cannot be released without it.
* TrustShield recipients bypass on-site ID capture; non-TrustShield recipients require active camera ID capture.
* GPS location and timestamp must be logged in the admin panel upon every age-restricted completion.
* The Customer Not Present timer is exactly 10 minutes. The Requestor must be notified immediately when the timer starts and must acknowledge the notification.
* The GPS proximity check at No Show submission uses a 50-foot (\~15 meter) radius from the drop-off lat/long. It is non-blocking but triggers a warning and fraud flag if the Gopher is outside the radius.
* Every Requestor No Show submission triggers a fraud alert in the admin panel regardless of GPS proximity.
* Tapping Requestor No Show triggers a mandatory 24-hour payout hold — this cannot be bypassed by the Gopher.
* Every Requestor No Show event must trigger an automated notification to admin@gophergo.io for monitoring.
* Confirmation Pending orders auto-complete after 24 hours if no admin action is taken.
* Admins may manually complete a Confirmation Pending order at any time to expedite payout.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* TrustShield status must be queryable at the time of completion to determine which verification branch to trigger.
* GPS and timestamp logging must be tied to the Continue action on the completion popup and to the Update – Completed action when Do Not Show Me Again is set.
* The 10-minute timer must send a push notification and SMS to the Requestor at the moment it starts, and must track whether the Requestor has acknowledged the notification.
* GPS proximity at No Show submission must be calculated against the drop-off location lat/long stored on the request record. The 50-foot radius (\~15 meters) accounts for large apartment complexes and multi-unit buildings.
* The fraud alert on No Show submission must create a flagged record in the admin panel linked to the order and the Gopher’s account.
* Automated email to admin@gophergo.io must fire on every Requestor No Show event.
* Admin panel must expose a manual Complete action on all Confirmation Pending orders.
* This ticket incorporates all requirements from G40-267 (No Show Update – Driver Must Be Near Drop-Off Location). G40-267 can be closed as a duplicate.
* Figma – Full flow: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=22-11153

Summary: Gopher Go — Prevent deletion of the last payout card on file to avoid Stripe account loss
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher managing my payout cards in Gopher Go,

## 🎯 I want

the system to prevent me from deleting my only card on file until I've added a replacement,

## ✅ So that

my Stripe account and full payout history are preserved and my future payouts are not disrupted.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* Currently, when a Gopher removes all cards on file, the Stripe account itself is deleted along with the entire payout history.
* This is unacceptable — the Stripe account and history must persist for the lifetime of the Gopher's account.
* The fix is to block deletion of the only card on file until a replacement card has been added.

---

## 🚫 Current Behavior

* A Gopher with only one payout card on file is able to delete that card.
* Doing so removes the last card from Stripe, which causes Stripe to delete the connected account.
* The deletion of the Stripe account wipes the full payout history.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* A Gopher must always have at least one payout card on file.
* If a Gopher attempts to delete their only card on file, the deletion is blocked and the following modal is displayed:

**Modal copy (per Figma):**

* **Title:** Attention!
* **Body:** Stripe requires a card on file in order to maintain your account history. Please add the new card and then you can delete the old one.
* **Primary button:** Back
* This rule applies regardless of card health — even an expired, declined, or otherwise invalid card cannot be removed until a replacement has been added.
* Once a new card is successfully added, the original card may be deleted without restriction.
* The Stripe account and payout history must remain intact through this entire flow.

---

## 🎨 Design Consideration / Open Question

The modal as designed only includes a **Back** button — there is no primary CTA that takes the Gopher directly to the Add New Card flow. Worth aligning with design on whether to:

* Add a primary **Add New Card** CTA that routes the Gopher to the card-add flow, with **Back** as a secondary action, **or**
* Keep the modal as-is and require the Gopher to navigate to Add New Card manually.

Recommendation is the first option — it reduces friction and aligns the user's next action with what the modal copy is asking them to do.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Block deletion of the only card**

* **Given** a Gopher has exactly one payout card on file,
* **When** the Gopher attempts to delete that card,
* **Then** the deletion is blocked and the "Attention!" modal is displayed.

**Scenario 2 — Add new card, then delete the original**

* **Given** a Gopher has dismissed the "Attention!" modal and added a valid new card,
* **When** the Gopher returns to delete the original card,
* **Then** the original card is successfully removed and the new card is the active payout method.

**Scenario 3 — Normal delete with multiple cards**

* **Given** a Gopher has two or more payout cards on file,
* **When** the Gopher deletes any card that is not the only card,
* **Then** the deletion succeeds without showing the modal, and at least one card remains on file.

**Scenario 4 — Stripe account preservation**

* **Given** a Gopher has only one payout card on file,
* **When** the deletion is blocked by the modal,
* **Then** the Gopher's Stripe account and full payout history remain intact and accessible.

**Scenario 5 — Bad card cannot be removed without replacement**

* **Given** a Gopher's only card on file is expired, declined, or otherwise invalid,
* **When** the Gopher attempts to remove that bad card,
* **Then** the deletion is still blocked and the modal is displayed.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* A Gopher must always have at least one payout card on file in Stripe — the count must never drop to zero through user action.
* The last-card check must run server-side before the Stripe detach API is called, not client-side only.
* The rule applies regardless of card health — valid, expired, declined, and otherwise invalid cards are all subject to the same block.
* Deleting the Stripe account or wiping payout history is never an acceptable side effect of a user action.
* The replacement flow must add the new card to the same Stripe account, not create a new one.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Reproduce by attempting to delete the only card on a test Gopher account — confirm the "Attention!" modal appears and the card is not removed.
* Confirm in the Stripe dashboard that the connected account and payout history are still present after the attempt.
* Add a second card, delete the original, and confirm the new card becomes the active payout method.
* Test with an expired or otherwise invalid card as the only card — confirm the block still applies.
* Test on both iOS and Android.
* Re-attach the modal screenshot directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URL does not render for other users).
* **Figma reference:** https://www.figma.com/design/g7DWLbI86O6SqiwITY7jeL/%E2%9C%8F%EF%B8%8F-Gopher-UI_UX?node-id=7046-28668

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* This bug is closely related to the payout-failure flow tickets — if a payout fails because the only card is invalid, the resolution path depends on the Gopher being able to add a replacement card. The block here ensures the Gopher cannot accidentally orphan their Stripe account during that recovery flow.
* Design alignment is needed on the "Add New Card" CTA question raised above before development begins.
