---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* When an admin deactivates a Gopher account, the system automatically calls Stripe to reject that Gopher's connected Stripe account — performing the same action the admin currently does manually in the Stripe dashboard.
* No manual admin step in Stripe is required.
* If the Stripe rejection call fails (Stripe API unreachable, account state issue, etc.), the deactivation event is logged as a partial success and surfaced to admin for manual retry. The Gopher account deactivation itself **does not** roll back.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — Deactivation triggers automatic Stripe rejection**

* **Given** an admin deactivates a Gopher account,
* **When** the deactivation is confirmed,
* **Then** the system calls Stripe and rejects the Gopher's connected Stripe account without any further manual admin action.

**Scenario 2 — Stripe account state matches manual rejection**

* **Given** the automatic rejection has run successfully,
* **When** an admin inspects the Stripe dashboard for that user,
* **Then** the connected account state is identical to what would have been produced by the existing manual rejection flow.

**Scenario 3 — Duplicate-detection logic remains intact**

* **Given** a Gopher's account has been deactivated and their Stripe account auto-rejected,
* **When** that user later attempts to create a new Stripe account with a different number,
* **Then** the existing duplicate-detection logic fires as it does today — no regression introduced.

**Scenario 4 — Stripe failure does not block deactivation**

* **Given** the Stripe API is unreachable or the rejection call fails,
* **When** the admin deactivates a Gopher account,
* **Then** the Gopher account is still deactivated, the partial failure is logged, and the admin is notified to retry the Stripe rejection manually.

**Scenario 5 — Re-activation is out of scope**

* **Given** a previously deactivated Gopher is later re-activated by an admin,
* **When** the re-activation occurs,
* **Then** this ticket makes no claim about what happens to the Stripe account — re-activation handling is out of scope.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* Deactivation is the **trigger** — every admin deactivation of a Gopher account fires the Stripe rejection.
* The Stripe rejection action must match the action currently performed manually in the Stripe dashboard — no new Stripe state should be introduced.
* A Stripe failure must not block the Gopher deactivation from succeeding.
* The existing duplicate-Stripe-detection logic must continue to fire after the auto-rejection — no behaviour change there.

---

## 🔎 Implementation Considerations

* The Stripe rejection should run **server-side** as part of the deactivation event handler, ideally in an async job so a slow Stripe response doesn't delay the admin's confirmation.
* Log every auto-rejection attempt (success or failure) with the account ID, Stripe account ID, timestamp, and result for audit.
* On failure, surface a retry action to admin so the manual fallback path stays available.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Deactivate a test Gopher account and confirm the connected Stripe account is rejected automatically, matching the state produced by the manual flow.
* Confirm the deactivation completes successfully even when the Stripe call is forced to fail (e.g., simulate Stripe API error) and the failure is logged + surfaced to admin.
* Confirm an existing duplicate-Stripe-detection test still passes after the auto-rejection.

Summary: Gopher Go — "Need A Ride" request details are missing rider count, special instructions, and trip distance on the Gopher view
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher Go user viewing an available "Need A Ride" request,

## 🎯 I want

to see all of the information relevant to the price offered and the job needed — including rider count, special instructions, and trip distance —

## ✅ So that

I can accept the request with confidence that I can perform everything required for the trip.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* When a "Need A Ride" request is submitted, the Requestor provides **Number of Riders** (required) and may provide **Special Instructions** (optional). The system also derives **Trip Distance** from the pickup → drop-off route.
* None of these three values currently appear on the Gopher's request details view.
* Without this information, the Gopher cannot confidently assess whether they can perform the trip (vehicle capacity, task constraints, effort vs. payout).

---

## 🚫 Current Behavior

* A Gopher viewing an available "Need A Ride" request does **not** see:

    * Number of Riders
    * Special Instructions (when provided)
    * Trip Distance (in miles)
    
* The Gopher must accept blind on these dimensions or message the Requestor to ask, which adds friction.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* The Gopher's request details view for "Need A Ride" must display all three values:

    * **Number of Riders** — always displayed (required at submission).
    * **Special Instructions** — displayed as full text when provided; the row is **omitted entirely** when not provided (not shown as an empty field).
    * **Trip Distance** — always displayed in **miles**, derived from the pickup → drop-off route.
    

---

## 📊 Missing-Fields Summary

| Field | In Requestor flow? | In Gopher view today? | Should show? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of Riders | Yes (required at submit) | No | Yes — always |
| Special Instructions | Yes (optional) | No | Yes, when provided (full text, omit row when empty) |
| Trip Distance (mi) | Derived from pickup → drop-off | No | Yes — always, in miles |

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 — All three fields visible on the Gopher request details view**

* **Given** a "Need A Ride" request has been submitted with rider count, special instructions, and a valid pickup/drop-off,
* **When** a Gopher views the request details before accepting,
* **Then** Number of Riders, Special Instructions (full text), and Trip Distance (in miles) are all displayed.

**Scenario 2 — Special Instructions omitted when not provided**

* **Given** a "Need A Ride" request was submitted without Special Instructions,
* **When** a Gopher views the request details,
* **Then** the Special Instructions row is omitted entirely (not shown as an empty field).

**Scenario 3 — Trip distance displays in miles**

* **Given** a "Need A Ride" request with valid pickup and drop-off addresses,
* **When** a Gopher views the request details,
* **Then** Trip Distance is shown in miles, calculated from the pickup → drop-off route.

**Scenario 4 — Number of Riders always displays**

* **When** a Gopher views the request details,
* **Then** Number of Riders is always populated with the value submitted (1 or more).

**Scenario 5 — Special Instructions display in full**

* **Given** a "Need A Ride" request was submitted with a long Special Instructions value,
* **When** a Gopher views the request details,
* **Then** the full text of Special Instructions is displayed without truncation or a "see more" affordance.

**Scenario 6 — Other request types unaffected**

* **Given** a Delivery or Service request is being viewed by a Gopher,
* **When** the Gopher views request details,

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* The Gopher's request details view must surface every field that materially affects the Gopher's ability to perform the request — vehicle capacity (riders), task constraints (special instructions), and effort (distance).
* Trip Distance is always displayed in **miles**, regardless of user locale.
* Special Instructions are always displayed in **full**, with no truncation or "see more" affordance.
* Optional fields with no value provided must be **omitted from the view entirely** — not shown as empty rows.
* Trip Distance is derived from the pickup → drop-off route and is read-only.
* This fix is scoped to the "Need A Ride" request type — Delivery and Service request types are not in scope but must be regression-tested.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Submit a "Need A Ride" request with no Special Instructions and confirm the row is omitted, not shown empty.
* Submit a "Need A Ride" request with a long Special Instructions value and confirm the full text displays without truncation.
* Validate Trip Distance against a known pickup → drop-off route to confirm calculation accuracy.
* Test on both iOS and Android.
* Run regression on Delivery and Service request views to confirm no unintended changes.
* Re-attach the "current state" and "should look" screenshots directly to this ticket (the existing `blob:` URLs do not render for other users) — or add a Figma link if a design exists.

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* This bug is a data-passing gap between the Requestor submit flow and the Gopher request details view — the values exist in the request payload but are not being read or rendered on the Gopher side.
* The fix may require both API and UI changes depending on whether the Gopher request details endpoint already includes these fields in its response.

Summary: Admin Panel - App Notifications / Inbox Message - Bulk Message Sending Error
Description:
The admin panel has lost the ability to send SMS , Inbox messages and push notifications to multiple users simultaneously. Two compounding issues exist: (1) selecting multiple users via comma-separated IDs and attempting to send results in an error, and (2) sending to large volumes of users causes major platform disruption. Both must be resolved so admins can reliably send push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS messages to any number of users without errors or server impact.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Admin Panel user,

## 🎯 I want

to be able to send push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS messages to any number of selected users without errors or platform disruption,

## ✅ So that

I can reliably communicate specific and targeted messages to individual users or large user groups at any time.

## 💡 Context / Background

* The admin panel previously supported sending push notifications and SMS messages to multiple users by entering their user IDs separated by commas.
* This functionality has regressed — users can be selected but attempting to send results in an error.
* A separate but related issue exists where sending to a large volume of users causes a major disruption to the platform, indicating the bulk send logic is not properly queued or rate-limited on the backend.
* The platform must support bulk sends of push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS messages to any number of users without negative server impact.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* Entering comma-separated user IDs and attempting to send a push notification or SMS results in an error — the message is not delivered
* Users can be selected in the admin panel but the send action fails
* Sending to a large number of users causes major platform disruption
* There is no rate-limiting, queuing, or batching in place to handle high-volume sends safely

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* Admins can select multiple users via comma-separated IDs and successfully send a push notification, inbox message, or SMS to all selected users
* No error is thrown during the send process regardless of the number of recipients
* Bulk sends of any volume are processed without causing server disruption or platform degradation
* Messages are queued and dispatched in batches on the backend to protect server stability

## ⚠️ Issue Breakdown

### Issue 1 – Multi-User Send Error

* Selecting multiple users via comma-separated IDs and attempting to send any message type returns an error
* This is a regression — the feature previously worked and must be restored
* Affects: push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS

### Issue 2 – Bulk Volume Causes Platform Disruption

* Sending to a large number of users simultaneously overwhelms the server and causes major platform disruption
* The backend send logic must be re-architected to use a queue-based or batch processing approach
* This is a critical scalability blocker — the platform must handle bulk sends of any size safely

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

### Issue 1 – Multi-User Send Error

1. Navigate to Admin Panel → App Notifications or Inbox Message.
2. Enter multiple user IDs separated by commas.
3. Compose a push notification, inbox message, or SMS.
4. Attempt to send.
5. Observe the error message and confirm the message was not delivered.

### Issue 2 – Bulk Volume Platform Disruption

1. Navigate to Admin Panel → App Notifications or Inbox Message.
2. Select a large volume of users.
3. Attempt to send a push notification, inbox message, or SMS.
4. Observe platform degradation or disruption.

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Multi-user send succeeds without error

* **Given** an admin enters multiple comma-separated user IDs and composes a message
* **When** the admin sends the message
* **Then** the message is successfully delivered to all selected users
* **And** no error is thrown

### Scenario 2 – All three message types work for multi-user sends

* **Given** an admin selects multiple users
* **When** the admin sends a push notification, inbox message, or SMS
* **Then** all three message types are successfully delivered to all selected users without error

### Scenario 3 – Large volume bulk send does not disrupt the platform

* **Given** an admin sends a message to a large number of users
* **When** the send is triggered
* **Then** messages are queued and dispatched in batches
* **And** no platform degradation, errors, or service disruption occurs
* **And** all recipients receive the message

### Scenario 4 – Single user send is unaffected by the fix

* **Given** an admin sends a message to a single user
* **When** the message is sent
* **Then** the message is delivered successfully with no change to the existing single-user send behavior

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* The admin panel must support sending push notifications, inbox messages, and SMS to any number of users without error.
* Bulk sends must never cause platform disruption regardless of recipient volume.
* Backend bulk send processing must use a queue-based or batch approach to protect server stability.
* Single-user send behavior must remain unchanged.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Identify the regression that broke multi-user comma-separated ID sending and restore the original behavior.
* Re-architect the bulk send backend to use a message queue (e.g. SQS, Redis queue, or equivalent) so large sends are processed asynchronously in batches rather than synchronously in a single request.
* Implement rate limiting and/or batch size caps on the notification dispatch layer to prevent server overload.
* Ensure the fix applies to all three message types: push notification, inbox message, and SMS.
* Consider adding a send progress indicator in the admin panel for large bulk sends so admins can confirm the send is processing.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Test sending a push notification, inbox message, and SMS to 2–5 comma-separated user IDs — confirm successful delivery with no error.
* Test sending to a large volume of users (e.g. 100, 500, 1000+) — confirm messages are delivered and no platform disruption occurs.
* Test all three message types for both small and large recipient lists.
* Test single-user send — confirm behavior is unchanged.
* Monitor server health and platform stability during large bulk send tests.
* Verify all recipients receive the message when sent in bulk.

Summary: Twilio SMS + Email backup escalation — exclude Gophers with no completed request in the last 6 months (with 3-month new-Gopher carve-out)
Description:
## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher operations system escalating a stalled request via Twilio SMS and Email backup,

## 🎯 I want

to exclude Gophers who have not completed any request in the last 6 months from receiving the escalation,

## ✅ So that

the escalation only reaches Gophers likely to act — reducing Twilio cost, recipient noise, and the rate of escalations that fail to convert because they hit dormant accounts.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* The Twilio SMS + Email **backup** communication is an **escalation channel** — it fires only when a submitted request has had **no activity for 5 minutes**.
* ⏱️ **Timer anchor (per G40-44):** the 5-minute window starts **AFTER the last broadcast notification has been sent** — i.e., after the final tier of the \[G40-44\] broadcast cadence has been notified — **not** at request submission. While the broadcast cadence is still sending notifications to tiers, the 5-minute inactivity clock has **not** started.
* The current escalation logic identifies a candidate list of nearby/qualified Gophers and sends them an SMS and Email in addition to (or in place of) the standard push.
* This ticket adds a **dormancy filter** on top of that existing candidate list: any candidate Gopher with **no completed request in the last 6 months** is removed from the SMS + Email send.
* Rationale: dormant Gophers are statistically unlikely to act on an escalation. Excluding them reduces Twilio spend, recipient fatigue, and stale-broadcast noise without changing the underlying candidate selection.

---

## 🔁 Where this filter inserts

1. Request is submitted; the **\[G40-44\] broadcast cadence** notifies worker tiers in sequence.
2. The **last broadcast notification** is sent (final tier reached).
3. **5 minutes elapse with no activity**, timed from that last-notification moment (**not** from submission).
4. Existing escalation logic identifies the candidate list of nearby/qualified Gophers (e.g., 50 Gophers).
5. **NEW — dormancy filter:** remove any candidate Gopher who (a) registered more than 3 months ago AND (b) has no completed request in the last 6 months. (e.g., 15 removed.)
6. Twilio sends SMS and Email to the remaining filtered list (e.g., 35 Gophers).

---

## 🧮 Worked Example

* Existing selection logic identifies **50** candidate Gophers for an escalation.
* Of those, **15** have no completed request in the last 6 months **and** registered more than 3 months ago.
* Dormancy filter excludes those 15.
* Final escalation list: **35** Gophers receive the SMS + Email backup.

---

## 🧪 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 0 — Timer starts after last broadcast notification**

* **Given** a request whose broadcast cadence (G40-44) is still notifying worker tiers,
* **When** the final tier's notification has just been sent,
* **Then** the 5-minute inactivity countdown starts at that moment — not at submission — and the escalation only fires if 5 minutes then pass with no activity.

**Scenario 1 — Dormant Gopher excluded**

* **Given** a Gopher registered more than 3 months ago and has no completed request in the last 6 months,
* **When** a 5-minute-inactivity escalation fires and the recipient list is finalised,
* **Then** that Gopher is excluded from both the SMS and the Email send.

**Scenario 2 — Brand-new Gopher (within first 3 months) included**

* **Given** a Gopher registered less than 3 months ago and has no completed requests yet,
* **When** an escalation fires,
* **Then** that Gopher is included — the dormancy filter only applies after the Gopher has been registered for 3 months.

**Scenario 3 — Gopher between 3 and 6 months with no completions**

* **Given** a Gopher registered between 3 and 6 months ago and has no completed requests yet,
* **When** an escalation fires,
* **Then** that Gopher is **excluded** — they are past the 3-month carve-out and have no qualifying activity in the 6-month window.

**Scenario 4 — Recently-active Gopher included**

* **Given** a Gopher has at least one completed request within the last 6 months,
* **When** an escalation fires,
* **Then** that Gopher is included regardless of when they originally registered.

**Scenario 5 — Auto-reactivation on next completion**

* **Given** a previously excluded Gopher completes a new request,
* **When** the next escalation occurs,
* **Then** the Gopher is automatically re-included — no manual reactivation is required.

**Scenario 6 — Cancelled and refunded orders do not reset the clock**

* **Given** a Gopher's only recent activity is a cancelled, refunded, expired, or admin-overridden order,
* **When** the dormancy filter evaluates their record,
* **Then** that activity does not count toward the 6-month window and the Gopher remains excluded.

**Scenario 7 — Worked example math**

* **Given** the existing selection logic returns 50 candidates and 15 are dormant per this rule,
* **When** the new filter is applied,
* **Then** exactly 35 Gophers receive the SMS + Email backup.

**Scenario 8 — Existing selection logic unchanged**

* **Given** the existing escalation candidate-selection logic was producing a candidate list of N Gophers before this change,
* **When** the new filter is applied,
* **Then** the underlying selection logic still produces the same N candidates — the filter only narrows that list, never expands or reorders it.

---

## 📐 Business Rules

* ⏱️ **Timer anchor:** the 5-minute inactivity window is measured from when the **last broadcast notification was sent** (final tier of the \[G40-44\] cadence), **not** from request submission. If the cadence is still sending notifications, the 5-minute clock has not started.
* The dormancy filter only runs on the **5-minute inactivity escalation path** — it does not affect push, marketing, transactional, or admin-triggered sends.
* The 6-month window is rolling — measured from the escalation timestamp, not a fixed calendar date.
* **"Completed"** means a request reached the successful Completed status. Cancelled, refunded, expired, and admin-overridden orders do **not** count toward the activity window.
* Gophers who registered **less than 3 months ago** are exempt from the filter — they have not had enough time on the platform to accumulate a completion history.
* Exclusion is automatic and reversible — the moment an excluded Gopher completes a new request, they re-enter the eligible pool for future escalations.
* The filter is **additive** to existing escalation logic — it does not change which Gophers are considered candidates, only which of those candidates are sent to.
* The filter must be applied to both the SMS and Email channels uniformly — a Gopher excluded from SMS is also excluded from Email for the same escalation.

---

## 📊 Observability

* Each escalation should log: total candidates identified by the upstream selection logic, count excluded by the new dormancy filter, and final send count.
* These counts should be retrievable in the admin panel or via an internal metrics endpoint to validate the filter is operating as expected and to track Twilio cost reduction over time.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Seed test Gophers with a known mix of registration dates and completed-request dates:

    * Registered 2 months ago, no completions — expect **included** (within 3-month carve-out).
    * Registered 4 months ago, no completions — expect **excluded** (past carve-out, no qualifying activity).
    * Registered 1 year ago, completed a request 5 months ago — expect **included**.
    * Registered 1 year ago, completed a request 7 months ago — expect **excluded**.
    * Registered 1 year ago, only cancelled/refunded orders in last 6 months — expect **excluded**.
    
* Submit a test request, let the broadcast cadence finish sending its last tier notification, then allow it to sit idle for 5 minutes from that point, and verify the SMS and Email recipient lists match the expected filtered set.
* Complete a request as a previously excluded Gopher and confirm they are re-included in the next escalation.
* Verify the observability counts are written correctly for at least one production-scale escalation.
* Confirm the underlying recipient-selection logic was not modified — its output count should be identical to pre-change for the same input.

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* **Relates to \[G40-44\] (Broadcast Cadence).** The "last notification sent" event that starts this 5-minute timer is the final-tier notification defined in G40-44. If G40-44's cadence changes, revisit this timer anchor.
* This filter depends on access to two data points per Gopher: registration date and most-recent successful completion date. Both should already exist in the Gopher record; if either is not currently exposed to the escalation service, that integration work is in scope.
* Recommend deploying behind a feature flag so the filter can be toggled off quickly if it over-restricts in production.

Summary: Gopher App – Request Again must carry over original order's address + photos/media
Description:
> 🔄 **RE-SCOPED 2026-07-02.** The original “Request Again behaves like Edit / errors on submit” bug **and** the forward/back-compat rules are **already solved by design in the new build** (`gopher-request.html` → `raFast` / `__startRequestAgainFast`): it builds a brand-new request via `resetFlowState()` + selective prefill, lands on Review, never references the prior order ID, silently ignores unknown old fields, and leaves new fields blank for validation. Code trace is in the comments. **The only remaining go-forward work is what this ticket now covers: carry the original order's ADDRESSES _and_ PHOTOS/MEDIA into the pre-filled Request Again.**

---

## 🎯 Requirement

When a user taps **Request Again** on a completed order, the new pre-filled request must carry over from the original order:

1. **Pickup & drop-off address(es)** — every stop, in the same order.
2. **Photos / media attachments.**

…as **editable** pre-filled values on the NEW request (the user may change or remove them before submitting).

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

**AC1 — Address carry-over.** Given a completed Delivery/Restaurant order with pickup + drop-off addresses, when the user taps Request Again, then the new request pre-fills all pickup and drop-off stops in the same order, the user can edit them, and submission succeeds. _(Fixes the Jan-23 QA defect where the drop-off address failed to load — order #496.)_

**AC2 — Media carry-over.** Given a completed order that included photos/media, when the user taps Request Again, then those photos are attached to the new request (shown, removable) and ride through on submit. _(Fixes the Jan-23 QA defect where the image did not carry over — compare orders #493 vs #494.)_

**AC3 — Copies, never linked.** The carried-over address/media are **copies** on the new order; editing or removing them must never touch the original completed order, which remains immutable.

**AC4 — Graceful when absent.** If the original order had no media (or an address type the current flow doesn't use), the corresponding field is simply left blank — no error. (Consistent with the already-implemented S6/S7 compat behavior.)

## 🛠️ Where this plugs in (go-forward)

* **Data / backend:** the completed-order (history) record must **persist the original order's addresses and media** so Request Again can read them. _(In today's prototype the history record —_ `DASH_DATA.previousRequests` — stores only date/id/category/details/worker/amount/rating/breakdown; it has no address or media fields, which is exactly why raFast doesn't yet carry them.)
* **Front-end:** extend `__startRequestAgainFast(prev, selected)` (`gopher-request.html:14320`) to map `prev` pickup/drop-off stops into `state.pickupStops` / `state.dropoffStops` — the `__startDealRequest` bridge already does exactly this pattern — and to attach `prev` media. **NOTE:** the flow `state` currently has **no** media/photos field at all; production must add one.

## ✅ Already handled — do NOT rebuild (verified in the new build)

* New order, new order ID, no edit, no linkage to the prior order (orig. S1/S2/S5).
* No “Update it” / edit copy anywhere (orig. S3).
* Submits without error on valid input (orig. S4).
* Obsolete cached fields silently ignored (orig. S6) and new required fields left blank + validated (orig. S7) — both inherent to the selective-prefill + land-on-Review pattern.

---

## 📋 Original bug context (historical — for reference)

Reported as: “Request Again” behaved like Edit Request (UI said “Update it”), referenced the previous order ID, and errored on submit instead of creating a new order. Repro: Account → Request History → Completed → Request Again → submit. Core behavior was QA-approved in STAGE/QA on 2026-01-29 (new order ID generated, original unchanged, no linkage, iOS + Android). The two carry-over defects above were raised in the 2026-01-23 QA return and are what remains.

Summary: Both Apps - Implement mandatory app update for future major release versions
Description:
**As a** user running an outdated major version of the app,

**I want** to be clearly prompted to update,

**So that** I can continue using a stable, compatible version of the app without encountering bugs or broken functionality caused by version mismatches.

---

## 💡 Context / Background

* Users are not currently required to upgrade to the latest version of the app.
* This results in multiple app versions in circulation, inconsistent behavior, already-fixed bugs appearing to still exist, and increased support and QA complexity.
* To stabilize behavior and ensure compatibility, a **force-update mechanism** is needed for **future major release versions** (defined as an increment to the first version number, e.g. 3.x → 4.0).
* Minor and patch versions (e.g. 4.0 → 4.1, 4.1.0 → 4.1.1) are **not** subject to forced updates unless explicitly configured.
* Applies to both **Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go** apps.

---

## 🛠️ Proposed Solution

### Backend

* Introduce a version-check endpoint that receives the device's installed app version, compares it against the **minimum required version** stored in the database, and returns whether the version is **Allowed** or **Blocked**.
* Minimum required version must be configurable per platform (iOS / Android) **without requiring an app redeployment**.
* Backend is the source of truth for version enforcement.

### Frontend

* On app launch (and on resume from background), call the version validation endpoint.
* If the backend returns **Blocked**:

    * Display a **full-screen, non-dismissible modal**.
    * Block access to all app functionality.
    * Show clear messaging explaining an update is required.
    * Include a primary CTA: **Update App** — deep-linked to the correct App Store (iOS App Store or Google Play).
    
* If the backend returns **Allowed**, the user proceeds normally.
* Define fallback behavior for network failure during version check (e.g. allow entry but retry on next launch).

---

## ❌ Current Behavior

* Users can continue using outdated versions indefinitely.
* Incompatible versions coexist in production.
* Unexpected bugs and behavior occur due to version mismatches.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* Users on outdated major versions are blocked from using the app until they update.
* Only compatible versions are allowed to interact with the system.

---

## 🔁 Acceptance Criteria

**Scenario 1 – Version validation on app launch**

* **Given** the app is launched
* **When** the app sends its current version to the backend
* **Then** the backend validates it against the platform-specific minimum required version and returns Allowed or Blocked

**Scenario 2 – Force update required**

* **Given** the user's app version is below the required major version
* **When** the backend responds with Blocked
* **Then** a full-screen, non-dismissible update modal is displayed
* **And** the user cannot access any app functionality

**Scenario 3 – Redirect to App Store**

* **Given** the force update modal is displayed
* **When** the user taps **Update App**
* **Then** they are deep-linked to the correct App Store for their platform (iOS or Android)

**Scenario 4 – App usage allowed**

* **Given** the user's app version meets or exceeds the minimum required version
* **When** the app completes version validation
* **Then** the user proceeds normally into the app with no interruption

**Scenario 5 – Platform-specific enforcement**

* **Given** the user is on iOS or Android
* **When** version validation occurs
* **Then** enforcement uses the minimum version configured specifically for that platform

**Scenario 6 – Network failure during version check**

* **Given** the app launches with no or poor network connectivity
* **When** the version check endpoint cannot be reached
* **Then** the app applies the defined fallback behavior (to be specified by the team before development begins)

---

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* Forced updates apply to **major version increments only** unless explicitly overridden in the backend config.
* The update modal must **not** be dismissible under any circumstance.
* Version requirements must be configurable per platform without an app redeployment.
* Backend is the single source of truth — the app must not make local version decisions.
* Applies to both **Gopher Request** and **Gopher Go**.

---

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Backend must expose a reliable, low-latency version-check endpoint.
* Frontend must perform version validation early in the app lifecycle, before any navigation.
* Fallback behavior for network failure must be defined and agreed upon before development begins.
* Modal copy must be clear and user-friendly — coordinate with design/copy team.

---

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Test with app versions below, equal to, and above the required major version.
* Verify the modal blocks all navigation and cannot be dismissed.
* Confirm the Update App CTA deep-links correctly on both iOS and Android.
* Test on both platforms with good, poor, and no network connectivity.
* Validate that backend version config changes take effect without an app release.

Summary: Infrastructure – Elastic Beanstalk Platform Upgrade & EC2-Classic → VPC Migration
Description:
‌

## **🧑‍💻 As a(n)**

engineer / platform / DevOps team,

## **🎯I want**

to upgrade our Elastic Beanstalk environment to a supported platform branch and migrate from EC2-Classic to VPC,

## **✅ So that**

we can continue making environment changes, receive security updates, and avoid deployment failures.

‌

## **💡 Context / Background**

‌

While attempting to update environment variables, AWS is blocking changes and displaying warnings indicating that the environment is running on **retired infrastructure**.

‌

Key issues identified:

‌

1️⃣ **Retired Elastic Beanstalk Platform**

* The environment uses a **retired platform branch**
* Retired branches:

    * No longer receive maintenance or security updates
    * Are not supported by AWS
    
* AWS recommends upgrading immediately.

Reference:

<custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/platforms-glossary.html</custom> 

‌

2️⃣ **Environment Created in EC2-Classic**

* The environment was originally created using **EC2-Classic**
* AWS now supports **VPC-only networking**
* When attempting to update environment variables:

    * Elastic Beanstalk tries to implicitly migrate networking
    * The update fails
    

This is likely the **root cause of deployment and configuration update failures**.

‌

## **❌ Current Behavior**

‌

* Updating environment variables fails.
* Infrastructure attempts to migrate automatically and errors out.
* Platform branch is unsupported and not receiving updates.
* Deployment and configuration changes are becoming risky/unreliable.

‌

## **✅ Expected Behavior**

‌

* Environment runs on a **supported Elastic Beanstalk platform branch**.
* Environment is fully migrated to **VPC networking**.
* Environment variables and configuration changes can be applied normally.
* Deployments succeed without platform or networking conflicts.

‌

## **🔍 Scope of Work**

‌

This ticket includes **research, planning, and migration execution**.

‌

### **Phase 1 – Assessment**

* Identify:

    * Current platform branch
    * Current runtime versions
    * Current EC2-Classic configuration
    
* Document:

    * Dependencies and risks
    * Downtime considerations
    * Required AWS resources (VPC, subnets, security groups)
    

    



### **Phase 2 – Migration Strategy**

* Plan migration to:

    * Supported Elastic Beanstalk platform
    * VPC networking
    
* Determine safest approach:

    * Blue/Green deployment (recommended)
    * New environment creation + cutover
    

    



### **Phase 3 – Implementation**

* Create new EB environment in VPC.
* Configure networking and security groups.
* Deploy application to new environment.
* Validate functionality.
* Cut over traffic (DNS swap).

‌

## **✅ Acceptance Criteria** 

‌

### **Scenario 1 – Platform branch upgraded**

* **Given** the new environment is created
* **When** the application is deployed
* **Then** the environment runs on a supported Elastic Beanstalk platform

‌

### **Scenario 2 – Environment migrated to VPC**

* **Given** the migration is complete
* **When** reviewing networking configuration
* **Then** the environment runs fully inside a VPC

‌

### **Scenario 3 – Configuration updates succeed**

* **Given** the new environment is active
* **When** updating environment variables
* **Then** the changes apply successfully without errors

‌

### **Scenario 4 – Successful deployment**

* **Given** traffic is routed to the new environment
* **When** users access the application
* **Then** the app behaves as before with no regression

‌

## **⚙️ Business Rules**

‌

* Must move off retired platform immediately.
* Must use VPC networking (AWS requirement).
* Prefer **zero-downtime migration**.
* Old environment should remain available until cutover validation is complete.

‌

## **🧠 Dependencies / Notes**

‌

* Requires AWS access and DevOps coordination.
* Recommend Blue/Green deployment to minimize risk.
* Verify:

    * Environment variables
    * S3 / RDS / external service connectivity
    * SSL / DNS configuration
    
* Old environment should be decommissioned only after validation.

‌

## **🧪 QA Notes**

‌

* Validate:

    * App loads and core flows work
    * Environment variables apply successfully
    * Deployments succeed
    
* Monitor logs after cutover.

Summary: BUG - Admin Panel - Deleted/Deactivated Date Issue
Description:
When running the User report in the admin panel, the Deleted/Deactivated date field incorrectly displays the account’s Created date instead of the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated. This makes it impossible to accurately track user churn, attrition, or account lifecycle in reporting.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

admin running the User report,

## 🎯 I want

the Deleted/Deactivated date field to show the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated,

## ✅ So that

I can accurately track user churn and attrition over time.

## 💡 Context / Background

* The User report in the admin panel includes a Deleted/Deactivated date field intended to track when an account was removed or disabled.
* This date is used to measure user churn and attrition over time.
* Currently, the field is incorrectly populated with the account’s Created date rather than the date the account was actually deleted or deactivated.
* This means all attrition reporting is currently inaccurate — deleted accounts appear as if they were deleted on the same day they were created.

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. In the admin panel, navigate to Reports → User report.
2. Filter or locate accounts with a Deleted or Deactivated status.
3. Observe the Deleted/Deactivated date column.
4. Confirm the date shown matches the account’s Created date rather than the actual deletion or deactivation date.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* The Deleted/Deactivated date field in the User report displays the account’s Created date
* The actual date the account was deleted or deactivated is not being recorded or displayed
* Attrition and churn reporting is inaccurate as a result

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* The Deleted/Deactivated date field in the User report displays the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated
* The Created date and Deleted/Deactivated date are stored and displayed as separate, distinct values
* Attrition and churn reports accurately reflect when users left the platform

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Deleted/Deactivated date shows the correct date

* **Given** an account has been deleted or deactivated
* **When** an admin views the User report
* **Then** the Deleted/Deactivated date field shows the actual date the account was deleted or deactivated
* **And** the date is different from the Created date unless the account was deleted on the same day it was created

### Scenario 2 – Created date is unaffected

* **Given** an account has been deleted or deactivated
* **When** an admin views the User report
* **Then** the Created date field still shows the original account creation date and is unchanged

### Scenario 3 – Active accounts show no Deleted/Deactivated date

* **Given** an account is active and has not been deleted or deactivated
* **When** an admin views the User report
* **Then** the Deleted/Deactivated date field is empty or null for that account

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* The Deleted/Deactivated date must always reflect the timestamp of the delete or deactivate action, not the account creation timestamp.
* Created date and Deleted/Deactivated date must be stored as separate fields in the data model.
* Active accounts must have a null or empty Deleted/Deactivated date.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Identify whether the Deleted/Deactivated date is stored as a separate field or is being incorrectly defaulted to the Created date at the report query layer.
* If the deletion/deactivation timestamp is not currently being recorded when an account is deleted or deactivated, a new field (e.g. deleted_at or deactivated_at) must be added to the user record and populated at the time of the action.
* Existing deleted/deactivated accounts with incorrect dates will need to be assessed — if the correct timestamps are not recoverable from logs, those records may need to remain as-is with a note that historical data prior to this fix may be inaccurate.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Delete or deactivate a test account and immediately check the User report — confirm the Deleted/Deactivated date reflects today’s date (the actual action date).
* Confirm the Created date for the same account is unchanged.
* Check an active account in the User report — confirm the Deleted/Deactivated date field is empty or null.
* Verify the fix applies to both deleted and deactivated account states.

Summary: BUG - Gopher App - Duplicate Issue - If User Edits Request To A Different Category, A New Request Is Generated
Description:
When a user edits an existing request — even if they change the subcategory — the original order number must be preserved. A new request must **never** be generated as a result of an edit.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher App user editing an existing request,

## 🎯 I want

my edited request to update in place and retain its original order number,

## ✅ So that

I do not end up with duplicate orders or lose track of my original request.

## 💡 Context / Background

* Users are able to edit a pending/active request from within the app.
* Editing within the **same subcategory** works correctly — the order number is retained and no duplicate is created.
* However, if the user changes to a **different subcategory** during an edit, the system incorrectly generates a **new request with a new order number**, resulting in a duplicate.
* Example: a user edits a _Delivery – General Errand_ request and changes it to _Delivery – Other Age-Restricted_. Instead of updating the existing order, a duplicate request is created.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* Editing a request and changing the subcategory causes the system to generate a **new order with a new order number**
* The original order remains open, resulting in a **duplicate request**
* Editing within the same subcategory does **not** trigger this issue — the bug is isolated to cross-subcategory edits

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* Any edit to a request — regardless of whether the subcategory changes — must **update the existing order in place**
* The **original order number is always retained**
* No new order or duplicate is ever created as a result of an edit
* The edit flow behaves consistently whether the subcategory stays the same or changes

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a request under any subcategory (e.g. _Delivery – General Errand_).
2. Navigate to the request and tap **Edit**.
3. Change the subcategory to a different one (e.g. _Delivery – Other Age-Restricted_).
4. Submit the edited request.
5. Observe that a new order number is generated and a duplicate request exists.

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Edit within the same subcategory

* **Given** a user edits a request without changing the subcategory
* **When** the edited request is submitted
* **Then** the original order is updated in place
* **And** the order number remains unchanged
* **And** no duplicate request is created

### Scenario 2 – Edit with a subcategory change

* **Given** a user edits a request and changes it to a different subcategory
* **When** the edited request is submitted
* **Then** the original order is updated in place with the new subcategory
* **And** the order number remains unchanged
* **And** no new order or duplicate is generated

### Scenario 3 – No duplicate in request history

* **Given** a user has submitted an edited request with a subcategory change
* **When** the user views their request history
* **Then** only one order exists for that request
* **And** the order reflects the updated subcategory

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* An edit to an existing request must **always update the original order** — never create a new one.
* The order number is immutable once assigned and must persist through any edits, including subcategory changes.
* Subcategory changes are treated as field-level updates, not new request creation events.
* Edit behavior must be consistent across all category and subcategory combinations.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Investigate whether a subcategory change triggers a new request creation event on the frontend or backend.
* Confirm the edit flow uses an **Update Request** endpoint, not a **Create Request** endpoint, for all edits regardless of subcategory.
* Ensure the original order ID is passed through the entire edit flow and is not reset upon subcategory selection.
* Verify fix is consistent across all category and subcategory combinations.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Test editing a request without changing the subcategory — confirm order number is retained.
* Test editing a request and changing to a different subcategory — confirm order number is retained and no duplicate is created.
* Test across multiple category and subcategory combinations.
* Verify request history shows only one order after an edit.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Saving An Order Info So Users Don't Have To Start Over (and learn user behaviors)
Description:
During order creation, users currently lose all entered data if they exit the app, switch screens, or are interrupted before submitting. This ticket introduces a Draft Order system that auto-saves order progress at every step, assigns a draft order number immediately when an order is started, and allows users to seamlessly resume where they left off. Draft order data is visible to the user in their order history, surfaced in a new admin panel tab, and used to build behavioral analytics around user drop-off and completion patterns. This feature is part of the new UI/UX version.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Requestor creating an order in the Gopher App,

## 🎯 I want

my order progress to be automatically saved as I move through each step so I can resume it if I leave the app or get interrupted,

## ✅ So that

I never have to start an order from scratch again, and the platform can better understand how users interact with the request creation flow.

## 💡 Context / Background

* Users currently lose all order creation progress if they leave the app, are interrupted, or navigate away before submitting. This creates friction and results in abandoned orders that are never completed.
* The Draft Order system addresses this by saving order data incrementally as the user progresses through each screen.
* A draft order number is assigned as soon as the user begins creating an order, before submission.
* Draft orders are surfaced to the user in their order history so they can find and resume them easily.
* Draft order data is also captured in a new admin panel tab and report, enabling the team to analyze where users drop off in the creation flow and understand behavioral patterns on the platform.
* This feature is part of the new UI/UX version.

## 🔀 Complete Flow

### Step 1 - Draft Order Created on First Interaction

* As soon as a user begins creating a request, a draft order number is assigned
* The draft order is immediately recorded in the user's order history and in the admin panel Draft Orders tab

### Step 2 - Auto-Save on Each Step

* Each time the user taps Next or transitions between screens during order creation, the data entered on that screen is saved to the draft
* Progress is preserved even if the user exits the app, backgrounds it, or navigates away before submitting

### Step 3 - Resume from Dashboard

* If the user leaves the app or navigates away at any point, tapping the Request button on the bottom dashboard nav shows the user their pending draft order(s)
* The user can select a draft and resume from the exact step where they left off
* Multiple drafts are supported - if a user has more than one pending draft, all are shown

### Step 4 - Draft Converts to Order on Submission

* When the user completes all steps and submits the request, the draft order is converted to a live order
* The draft order record is updated with the final submitted status

### Step 5 - Cancelled Draft Orders are Retained

* If a user cancels a draft order, the draft is retained in the log with a final status of Cancelled
* The data entered up to the point of cancellation is preserved for analytics purposes

## 📄 Draft Orders - User-Facing

* Draft orders appear in the user's Order History tab, clearly labeled as Draft
* Tapping the Request button on the dashboard when a draft exists shows the user their pending draft(s) first
* The user can resume a draft or start a new request

## 📊 Draft Orders - Admin Panel

* A new Draft Orders tab is added to the admin panel
* The Draft Orders report mirrors the existing Orders report but includes two additional columns: Pending (draft not yet submitted) and Cancelled (draft cancelled before submission)
* Draft order records are also visible in individual user profiles in the admin panel
* Draft data is retained permanently for behavioral analytics, even after the draft is converted or cancelled

## ❌ Current Behavior

* No order progress is saved during creation - if the user exits the app or navigates away, all entered data is lost
* Users must start the entire order creation flow from scratch after any interruption
* No draft order tracking exists in the user-facing UI or admin panel

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 - Draft order number is assigned on first step

* **Given** a user begins creating a request
* **When** the first step of the order creation flow is initiated
* **Then** a draft order number is assigned and the draft is recorded in the system

### Scenario 2 - Progress is saved on each Next tap

* **Given** a user is progressing through order creation
* **When** the user taps Next or transitions to the next screen
* **Then** all data entered on the current screen is saved to the draft

### Scenario 3 - User can resume draft after leaving the app

* **Given** a user has a pending draft and has left the app
* **When** the user taps the Request button on the dashboard
* **Then** the user's pending draft(s) are shown and they can resume from the step where they left off

### Scenario 4 - Submitted draft converts to a live order

* **Given** a user completes all order creation steps and submits
* **When** the order is submitted
* **Then** the draft is converted to a live order and no longer appears as a pending draft

### Scenario 5 - Cancelled draft is retained with Cancelled status

* **Given** a user cancels a draft order
* **When** the cancellation is confirmed
* **Then** the draft record is retained with a final status of Cancelled and all data is preserved for analytics

### Scenario 6 - Draft orders appear in user Order History

* **Given** a user has one or more pending draft orders
* **When** the user views their Order History
* **Then** the drafts are clearly visible and labeled as Draft

### Scenario 7 - Admin panel Draft Orders tab shows all draft records

* **Given** draft orders exist on the platform
* **When** an admin navigates to the Draft Orders tab
* **Then** all draft orders are listed with Pending and Cancelled columns visible

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* A draft order number is assigned at the start of every order creation session.
* Progress is saved incrementally at every Next tap or screen transition - no manual save action is required from the user.
* Draft orders are accessible from the Request button on the dashboard and from the user's Order History.
* A draft is converted to a live order only upon final submission.
* Cancelled drafts are never deleted - they are retained with a Cancelled status for analytics.
* Draft order data is visible in individual user profiles in the admin panel.
* The admin panel Draft Orders report mirrors the Orders report and includes Pending and Cancelled status columns.
* This feature is part of the new UI/UX version and should be scoped and implemented accordingly.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* A draft order data model must be created with fields for: draft order number, user ID, category/subcategory, all order creation fields captured per step, current step, status (Pending / Converted / Cancelled), created timestamp, last updated timestamp.
* The draft must be saved to the backend on each Next action - local device storage alone is not sufficient as the user must be able to resume on any device.
* The Request button on the dashboard must check for existing pending drafts and surface them before launching a new creation flow.
* The admin panel requires a new Draft Orders tab and report, plus a Draft Orders section in individual user profiles.
* Draft order analytics will enable the team to identify drop-off points in the creation flow by measuring which step users most commonly abandon - the last saved step on cancelled or stale drafts is the key metric.
* This feature is part of the new UI/UX version - implementation must align with the new design system and flow.
* Figma design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=102-13675

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Start creating an order and tap Next through several steps - confirm a draft order number is assigned and data is saved at each step.
* Exit the app mid-creation, reopen, and tap the Request button - confirm the pending draft is shown and the flow resumes from the last saved step.
* Complete and submit an order - confirm the draft converts to a live order and is no longer listed as a pending draft.
* Cancel a draft mid-creation - confirm it is retained in the log with Cancelled status.
* Check the user's Order History - confirm drafts are visible and clearly labeled.
* Check the admin panel Draft Orders tab - confirm all drafts appear with Pending and Cancelled columns.
* Check the user's profile in the admin panel - confirm their draft orders are visible.
* Create multiple drafts without submitting - confirm all appear when the Request button is tapped.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: BUG - Both Apps - Sign-Up Issue With Existing Users
Description:
Following the sign-up process enhancement deployed to the App Stores in March 2026, multiple issues have emerged affecting existing users with unconfirmed email addresses, admin panel email management, and AWS authentication sync. These issues span both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

returning user, admin, or support team member,

## 🎯 I want

existing user accounts to be correctly recognized and manageable across the app and admin panel,

## ✅ So that

users are not forced into unwanted new account creation, email updates are properly synced, and confirmation flows work as intended.

## 💡 Context / Background

* In March 2026, a sign-up process enhancement was deployed to both app stores.
* This enhancement introduced regressions affecting existing users with unconfirmed email addresses.
* A new user category was added in AWS that is not linked to the admin panel, creating a sync disconnect.
* The issues affect both the user-facing apps and the admin panel's ability to manage accounts.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* Existing users with unconfirmed email addresses are being **forced to create new accounts**, even if they have existing order history
* These users should instead be prompted to **update their email address and confirm via OTP** — this flow is not triggering correctly
* A new AWS category introduced during the March 2026 deployment is **not linked to the admin panel** — email changes made in the admin panel are no longer recognized by the app
* When an admin manually updates a user’s email address in the admin panel, the change is **not saved in a way the app recognizes**
* The **Send Confirmation Email** button in the admin panel is not functioning correctly following the March 2026 deployment
* If a user begins sign-up, reaches the email OTP screen, and **does not complete the session** (OTP expires or session is abandoned), the next time they log in via SMS they are immediately shown the email OTP screen again
* On the email OTP screen, tapping the **back arrow (upper left)** simply refreshes the same OTP page — it does not navigate back
* The user has no way to update their email address or resend the OTP if the email on file is incorrect — they are completely stuck

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* Existing users with unconfirmed emails are **never forced into new account creation** — their existing account and order history must be preserved
* These users are prompted to **update and confirm their email via OTP** within the existing account flow
* The new AWS category is **fully linked to the admin panel** so that email updates made by admins are recognized by the app
* Admin panel email updates are **saved and synced correctly** so the app recognizes the change immediately
* The **Send Confirmation Email** button functions correctly and sends the confirmation email to the user
* When a user re-logs in via SMS and is shown the email OTP screen, the **back arrow navigates back to the Confirmation screen** where they can update their email address
* From the Confirmation screen, the user can **correct their email address and trigger a new OTP** to be sent

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

### Issue 1 – Existing user forced into new account creation

1. Identify an existing user with an unconfirmed email address and order history.
2. Attempt to log in or resume the account on either app.
3. Observe that the user is routed to new account creation instead of an email update/OTP confirmation flow.

### Issue 2 – Admin panel email update not recognized by app

1. In the admin panel, manually update a user's email address.
2. Attempt to log in with the updated email on either app.
3. Observe the app does not recognize the updated email.

### Issue 3 – Send Confirmation Email button not working

1. In the admin panel, navigate to a user account.
2. Click the Send Confirmation Email button.
3. Observe the email is not sent or the button produces no action.

### Issue 4 – User stuck on email OTP screen after incomplete session

1. Begin sign-up and proceed all the way to the email OTP screen.
2. Do not complete the OTP entry — exit the app or allow the session to expire.
3. Log back in using SMS.
4. Observe the email OTP screen is shown immediately.
5. Tap the back arrow (upper left).
6. Observe the same OTP page refreshes instead of navigating back.
7. Observe there is no way to update the email address or request a new OTP.

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Existing user with unconfirmed email is not forced into new account creation

* **Given** an existing user with an unconfirmed email address and order history attempts to access their account
* **When** the app recognizes the existing account
* **Then** the user is prompted to update and confirm their email via OTP
* **And** their existing account and order history are preserved
* **And** no new account is created

### Scenario 2 – OTP email confirmation flow works correctly

* **Given** the user is prompted to confirm their email via OTP
* **When** the user enters the correct OTP
* **Then** the email is confirmed and the user gains full access to their account

### Scenario 3 – Admin panel email update is recognized by the app

* **Given** an admin has updated a user's email address in the admin panel
* **When** the user attempts to log in with the updated email
* **Then** the app recognizes the updated email and allows login

### Scenario 4 – Send Confirmation Email button works correctly

* **Given** an admin clicks the Send Confirmation Email button for a user
* **When** the action is triggered
* **Then** a confirmation email is successfully sent to the user
* **And** the user receives the email and can complete confirmation

### Scenario 5 – AWS category is linked to the admin panel

* **Given** the new AWS user category exists
* **When** an email is updated via the admin panel
* **Then** the change is reflected in AWS and recognized by the app

### Scenario 6 – Back arrow on email OTP screen navigates to Confirmation screen

* **Given** a user is on the email OTP screen after logging in via SMS
* **When** the user taps the back arrow (upper left)
* **Then** the user is taken back to the Confirmation screen
* **And** the OTP page does not refresh

### Scenario 7 – User can update email and resend OTP from Confirmation screen

* **Given** a user has navigated back to the Confirmation screen from the OTP screen
* **When** the user updates their email address and re-submits
* **Then** a new OTP is sent to the updated email address
* **And** the user can complete email confirmation successfully

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* Existing users must never be forced into new account creation regardless of email confirmation status.
* Users with unconfirmed emails must be routed to an email update and OTP confirmation flow within their existing account.
* Email updates made in the admin panel must be synced to AWS and recognized by the app.
* The Send Confirmation Email button must function correctly at all times post sign-up enhancement.
* All AWS user categories must be linked to and manageable from the admin panel.
* The back arrow on the email OTP screen must always navigate back to the Confirmation screen — never refresh the OTP page.
* Users must always have a path to correct their email address and request a new OTP if needed.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Root cause is tied to the sign-up process enhancement deployed to the App Stores in March 2026 — regression introduced at that point.
* Investigate the new AWS user category added during the March 2026 deployment and confirm it is properly linked to the admin panel.
* Confirm the admin panel email update flow writes changes to the correct AWS attribute so the app can recognize them.
* Review and fix the Send Confirmation Email trigger in the admin panel to ensure it fires correctly post-deployment.
* Fix back arrow navigation on the email OTP screen so it routes to the Confirmation screen rather than refreshing in place.
* Applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.
* **Related tickets:** This bug is a direct result of the sign-up enhancement work defined in G40-7 (Frontend — Simplify Sign-Up Process) and G40-242 (Backend — Simplify Sign-Up Process). G40-7 and G40-242 define the intended front-end and back-end behavior; G40-271 captures the regressions introduced when that work was deployed. All three must be reviewed together.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Test with an existing user account that has an unconfirmed email — confirm the OTP update flow is triggered and no new account is created.
* Test admin panel email update — confirm the change is recognized by the app on next login.
* Test the Send Confirmation Email button — confirm the email is delivered and the user can complete confirmation.
* Verify the new AWS category is visible and manageable from the admin panel.
* Simulate an incomplete sign-up session (exit before OTP entry), log back in via SMS, and verify the back arrow on the OTP screen navigates to the Confirmation screen.
* From the Confirmation screen, update the email address and verify a new OTP is sent and confirmation completes successfully.
* Test on both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Admin Panel - Create an Email OTP field just like we have for SMS
Description:

With the introduction of email OTP verification, admins need an equivalent report for email OTPs to assist users with recovery. This ticket renames the existing OTP report to SMS OTP and creates a new Email OTP report that is an exact replica of the SMS OTP report.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Summary: Gopher App - Address Entered To Recognize Current Time Zones
Description:
The app currently determines time zone based solely on the user's device location. When a request involves an address in a different time zone, all scheduled times must be derived from and displayed relative to the time zone of the request address — not the user's device. This affects both how times are stored and how they are displayed to Requestors and Gophers across both apps.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Requestor scheduling a request at an address in a different time zone, or a Gopher viewing a scheduled request,

## 🎯 I want

all scheduled times to reflect the correct time zone for the request location, displayed accurately in my own local time,

## ✅ So that

neither the Requestor nor the Gopher is confused about when a scheduled request is supposed to occur, regardless of where each party is located.

## 💡 Context / Background

* The app currently uses the user's device time zone as the reference for all scheduling and time display.
* When a Requestor creates a scheduled request for an address in a different time zone, the scheduled time is incorrectly interpreted against the Requestor's device time zone rather than the address's time zone.
* This causes scheduling confusion for both parties, particularly when a Gopher is in a different time zone from the request address.
* The fix requires deriving the request time zone from the address, storing the canonical time in UTC, and displaying it converted to each party's local time zone.

## 📍 Time Zone Trigger Rules

* **Standard requests** — the time zone is derived from the pick-up address entered by the Requestor
* **"Gopher can pick up anywhere" selected** — when this option is chosen, no specific pick-up address is provided, so the drop-off address becomes the time zone trigger

## 🕒 How Times Must Be Displayed

* **Requestor** — sees the scheduled time in the time zone of the request address. Example: a request scheduled for 2:00 PM at a pick-up address in Chicago is shown to the Requestor as 2:00 PM CT.
* **Gopher (Gopher Go)** — sees the scheduled time converted to their own local time zone. Example: a Gopher in New York sees the same Chicago 2:00 PM CT request as 3:00 PM ET.
* A time zone label must always be shown alongside the scheduled time so both parties know which time zone is being referenced.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* All scheduled times are based on the device’s local time zone, regardless of the request address
* A request scheduled at an address in a different time zone displays the wrong local time to the Gopher
* No time zone label is shown alongside scheduled times

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* When a pick-up or drop-off address is entered in a different time zone, the app determines the time zone from that address
* The scheduled time is stored in UTC and displayed to each user converted to their relevant local time zone
* The Requestor sees the time in the request address time zone; the Gopher sees it converted to their own local time
* A time zone label is displayed alongside every scheduled time

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 - Pick-up address determines the request time zone

* **Given** a Requestor enters a pick-up address in a time zone different from their device
* **When** the Requestor schedules a future time for the request
* **Then** the time picker reflects the time zone of the pick-up address
* **And** the time zone label is shown alongside the scheduled time

### Scenario 2 - Drop-off address is the trigger when Gopher can pick up anywhere

* **Given** a Requestor selects "Gopher can pick up anywhere" and enters a drop-off address in a different time zone
* **When** the Requestor schedules a future time
* **Then** the time zone is derived from the drop-off address

### Scenario 3 - Gopher sees scheduled time in their own local time zone

* **Given** a scheduled request exists with a pick-up address in a different time zone from the Gopher
* **When** the Gopher views the request in Gopher Go
* **Then** the scheduled time is displayed converted to the Gopher’s local time zone with a time zone label

### Scenario 4 - Same time zone request is unaffected

* **Given** a Requestor enters an address in the same time zone as their device
* **When** they schedule a request
* **Then** the behavior is identical to the current experience with no change

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* The request time zone is always derived from the pick-up address. If no pick-up address is provided (Gopher can pick up anywhere), the drop-off address is used.
* Scheduled times must be stored in UTC on the backend.
* Times must be displayed to each user converted to their relevant local time zone — the Requestor sees the request address time zone; the Gopher sees their own device time zone.
* A time zone abbreviation or label must always be shown alongside any displayed scheduled time.
* This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Use the Google Time Zone API or equivalent to resolve the IANA time zone identifier from the pick-up or drop-off lat/long at the time the address is entered.
* Store the resolved IANA time zone on the request record alongside the UTC scheduled time so it can be used for accurate display on both sides.
* All existing scheduled request timestamps must be audited — if they are currently stored in local time rather than UTC, a migration plan is required.
* The time picker UI on the Requestor side must reflect the request address time zone, not the device time zone, when they differ.
* The Gopher Go app must convert the UTC scheduled time to the Gopher’s device time zone for display.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Create a scheduled request with a pick-up address in a different time zone — confirm the time picker reflects that address’s time zone and the label is shown.
* Select "Gopher can pick up anywhere" and enter a drop-off address in a different time zone — confirm the time zone is derived from the drop-off address.
* As a Gopher in a different time zone, view the scheduled request in Gopher Go — confirm the time is correctly converted to the Gopher’s local time zone with a label.
* Create a request with an address in the same time zone as the device — confirm no change in behavior.
* Test with addresses spanning multiple US time zones (ET, CT, MT, PT) to cover all offset scenarios.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

Summary: Gopher App - Regression Error - Flow Is Allowing Pick-Up and Drop-Off Address To Be The Same
Description:
The app is currently allowing users to submit a request where the pick-up and drop-off addresses are identical. This is a regression — this validation previously existed and must be restored. When a user enters the same address for both fields, a friendly in-app reminder must appear and prevent submission until the addresses are corrected.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher App user creating a request,

## 🎯 I want

to be clearly notified if my pick-up and drop-off addresses are the same,

## ✅ So that

I can correct the error before submitting and avoid a request that cannot be fulfilled.

## 💡 Context / Background

* Any request that involves a pick-up and drop-off location requires two distinct addresses.
* Having the same address for both fields is logically invalid and cannot be fulfilled by a Gopher.
* This validation was previously in place but has regressed — the app is now allowing identical addresses to pass through without any warning or error.
* A friendly, non-disruptive reminder popup must be shown to guide the user to fix the issue rather than a hard error block.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* The app allows a user to enter the same address for both pick-up and drop-off with no warning
* No validation or error message is triggered
* The request can proceed to submission with identical addresses

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* If a user enters the same address for both pick-up and drop-off, a **friendly reminder popup** is displayed
* The popup message clearly communicates that pick-up and drop-off addresses must be different
* The user is returned to the address fields to make a correction
* Submission is blocked until the two addresses are distinct
* This validation applies to all request types that include pick-up and drop-off fields

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin creating any request that includes pick-up and drop-off address fields.
2. Enter the same address in both the pick-up and drop-off fields.
3. Proceed to submit the request.
4. Observe that no warning or validation error appears and the request is allowed to proceed.

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – Same address entered for pick-up and drop-off

* **Given** a user has entered the same address for both pick-up and drop-off
* **When** the user attempts to proceed or submit
* **Then** a friendly reminder popup is displayed
* **And** the popup informs the user that pick-up and drop-off addresses must be different
* **And** submission is blocked until the addresses are corrected

### Scenario 2 – Different addresses entered for pick-up and drop-off

* **Given** a user has entered different addresses for pick-up and drop-off
* **When** the user attempts to proceed or submit
* **Then** no popup or validation error appears
* **And** the request proceeds normally

### Scenario 3 – User corrects addresses after reminder

* **Given** the reminder popup has been shown
* **When** the user updates one of the addresses to be different
* **Then** the validation clears and the user can proceed with submission

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* Pick-up and drop-off addresses must never be identical for any request type.
* Validation must trigger before submission is allowed to proceed.
* The user-facing message must be friendly and instructional, not a hard error block.
* This rule applies across all request types and flows that include pick-up and drop-off fields.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Reference Figma design for the reminder popup UI: https://www.figma.com/design/aRFH8dqUfSHLJTb89VZYNh/Jira-Tickets?node-id=103-14608
* Identify at which point in the previous build this validation existed and where the regression was introduced.
* Validation should ideally trigger on address field blur or on submission attempt — confirm preferred UX trigger with design.
* Ensure address comparison is normalized (e.g. case-insensitive, trimmed whitespace) to catch identical addresses entered with slight formatting differences.

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Test entering the exact same address in both pick-up and drop-off fields — confirm reminder popup appears and blocks submission.
* Test entering different addresses — confirm no popup and request proceeds normally.
* Test correcting the address after the popup appears — confirm validation clears and submission is allowed.
* Test with slight formatting variations of the same address (different casing, extra spaces) — confirm the validation still catches them as identical.
* Test across all request types that include pick-up and drop-off fields.
* Test on both iOS and Android.
