Summary: Both Apps - Convert Intercom And Inbox
Description:
Intercom is currently used for in-app customer support messaging in both the Gopher App and Gopher Go. When a support agent replies to a user through Intercom’s in-app messenger (not email-based threads), the user receives no dashboard notification or inbox alert within the app. This is not a replacement of Intercom — Intercom remains the messaging platform. The fix is to surface Intercom message notifications in the app’s existing inbox/notification system so users are alerted when a new Intercom reply is waiting for them.

## 🧑‍💻 As a

Gopher App or Gopher Go user who has an active Intercom support conversation,

## 🎯 I want

to receive an in-app inbox or dashboard notification when a support agent replies to my message,

## ✅ So that

I never miss a support reply and can respond promptly without having to manually check Intercom.

## 💡 Context / Background

* Intercom is used as the in-app support messaging platform across both apps and has accumulated 3 years of customer conversation history.
* This history is a valuable asset and will be leveraged for a future AI chatbot. Intercom is not being replaced.
* Currently, when a support agent sends a reply through Intercom’s in-app messenger, the user is not notified via the app’s inbox or dashboard. The message sits unread unless the user happens to open Intercom manually.
* This is specifically for Intercom’s in-app messenger conversations, not Intercom threads that have already moved to email.
* The solution is to use Intercom’s webhook or notification API to trigger an in-app inbox alert when a new reply is sent to the user through the in-app messenger.

## ❌ Current Behavior

* When a support agent replies to a user via Intercom’s in-app messenger, no dashboard alert or inbox notification is shown to the user in the app
* Users must manually open Intercom to check for new replies
* Response rates and resolution times are impacted because users are unaware of new replies

## ✅ Expected Behavior

* When a support agent sends a new reply through Intercom’s in-app messenger, the user receives an in-app inbox notification or dashboard alert
* The notification indicates a new message from support is waiting
* Tapping the notification takes the user directly to the Intercom conversation
* Intercom remains the messaging platform — no changes to how messages are stored, managed, or sent
* This does not apply to Intercom conversations that have transitioned to email threads

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

### Scenario 1 – User receives in-app notification when Intercom reply is sent

* **Given** a user has an active in-app Intercom conversation
* **When** a support agent sends a reply through Intercom’s in-app messenger
* **Then** the user receives an in-app inbox or dashboard notification alerting them to the new message

### Scenario 2 – Tapping the notification opens the Intercom conversation

* **Given** the user has received an in-app notification for a new Intercom reply
* **When** the user taps the notification
* **Then** the user is taken directly to the relevant Intercom conversation

### Scenario 3 – Email-transitioned conversations do not trigger in-app notifications

* **Given** an Intercom conversation has transitioned to an email thread
* **When** a reply is sent on that thread
* **Then** no in-app notification is triggered — the user is notified via email only as before

### Scenario 4 – Notification clears once the user views the message

* **Given** the user has an unread Intercom notification in their inbox
* **When** the user opens and reads the Intercom message
* **Then** the notification is marked as read and cleared from the inbox

## ⚙️ Business Rules

* Intercom remains the messaging platform — no messages are to be migrated, replaced, or duplicated.
* Notifications apply only to in-app Intercom messenger conversations, not email-transitioned threads.
* The notification must deep-link directly to the relevant Intercom conversation.
* This applies to both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.

## 🧠 Dependencies / Notes

* Use Intercom’s webhook integration to listen for the conversation.reply event and trigger an in-app notification when a new reply is sent to a user.
* Alternatively, Intercom’s Mobile Push Notifications SDK can be used to deliver push alerts natively when a new in-app message is received — evaluate which approach best fits the current integration.
* The notification payload must include the conversation ID so a deep link to the Intercom thread can be constructed.
* Confirm with the Intercom integration that conversations transitioned to email can be identified and excluded from triggering in-app notifications.
* Intercom’s 3 years of conversation history is not in scope for this ticket but will be leveraged in a future AI chatbot initiative — ensure no changes made here affect the historical data.
* Intercom webhook reference: https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/webhooks/
* Intercom Mobile Push reference: https://developers.intercom.com/installing-intercom/docs/ios-push-notifications

## 🧪 QA Notes

* Have a support agent send a reply via Intercom in-app messenger — confirm the user receives an in-app inbox or dashboard notification.
* Tap the notification — confirm it deep-links directly to the Intercom conversation.
* Send a reply on an email-transitioned Intercom thread — confirm no in-app notification is triggered.
* Open and read the Intercom message — confirm the notification clears from the inbox.
* Verify Intercom conversation history and existing functionality are unaffected.
* Test on both the Gopher App and Gopher Go.
* Test on both iOS and Android.

each new email template registered in the backend dispatcher and fired from the correct event, with net-new triggers built where none exist,

Summary: Gopher Request — Request-specific deep link into a specific request's cancel flow (replace deprecated Firebase Dynamic Links)
Description:
## 🎯 Goal

Provide a deep link that carries a **specific request id** and, when tapped, opens the Gopher Request app directly on **that request's cancel flow** (not the home screen, not a different request).

## 💡 Why this is its own ticket

Split out of **G40-108** (48-hour check-in email). Grounding finding: **no request-specific deep link exists anywhere in the backend today.** Every SMS/email link is a single static Firebase Dynamic Link — `https://gopherrequestapp.page.link/amTC` (requester) / `https://gophergoapp.page.link/H2PN` (gopher) — that opens the app generically and carries no order id (see `middleware/crons.js:389,557`, `controllers/order/cost_adjustment.js:195`, `controllers/order/order_bids.js:808`).

G40-108 ships v1 with the existing generic app-open link; this ticket is the **prerequisite** for its acceptance **Scenario 6** (and would upgrade the check-in email to true one-tap cancel).

## ⚠️ Platform constraint — Firebase Dynamic Links is deprecated

Google has **deprecated Firebase Dynamic Links (shutdown 2025)**. Do **not** extend FDL. This ticket should establish the **replacement** deep-link mechanism (iOS Universal Links / Android App Links, or an equivalent) for the whole platform — the request-specific cancel link is the first consumer.

## ✅ Expected behavior

* A link of the form "open request `<id>` → cancel flow" can be generated backend-side.
* Tapping it with the app installed routes to that specific request's cancel screen.
* Fallback (app not installed) behaves sanely (store / web landing).
* Reusable: other per-request notifications (bids, counter-offers, cost adjustments) can adopt the same request-scoped link.

## 🔗 Consumers / follow-on

* **G40-108** — 48h check-in email (blocked-by this for Scenario 6).
* Candidate migrations off the generic FDL: cost-adjustment SMS, confirm-reminder SMS, bid/counter-offer notifications.

## 🧠 Notes

Scope covers both (a) backend link generation carrying the order id and (b) app-side route handling that parses it and lands on the cancel flow. Verify on iOS + Android across Gmail / Apple Mail / Outlook.

Summary: Pop-up Modal Standards — establish + implement modal style guides (Request/Connect and the 2 native apps) BEFORE dev handoff
Description:
## Goal

Establish a canonical **pop-up / modal style guide** and reusable modal component, then implement it across the new-flow surfaces **before anything is handed to the new developer**. Every modal in the product should come from this standard — not from old Figma.

## Why (important fork)

The majority of the old Figma designs depict the **OLD UX**. We are **not** carrying any old-app Figma designs into the new build. Modal/pop-up UI must be defined fresh here and implemented in the prototypes so the developer builds against a single, consistent, already-realized standard instead of reverse-engineering inconsistent one-off modals or stale Figma frames.

## Two style guides

**Guide A — Request + Connect** (customer & business request surfaces)

* Source of truth: `Final/gopher-request.html` (`.gr-modal`) and `Final/gopher-connect.html` (`.gc-modal`).

**Guide B — The 2 native apps** (Gopher requester App + Gopher Go worker App)

* Source of truth: `_prototypes/Go/gopher-go-worker.html` and the requester app shell.

Each guide is derived from the **current new-UX prototypes**, harmonized — never from old Figma.

## Scope — what the standard must define (per guide)

1. **Anatomy:** scrim/overlay, container, close affordance, icon/illustration slot, eyebrow, title, body, primary CTA, secondary/text action.
2. **Variants:** info · confirm · success · warning/destructive · input.
3. **Sizing & responsive** behavior (mobile-first; safe-area on native).
4. **Typography** scale + brand fonts.
5. **Color tokens** (Midnight Blue #002461, Shamrock #33D975, Sand #FBF3E4, + accent), including destructive.
6. **Button hierarchy** (primary filled / secondary text) + placement.
7. **Motion** (enter/exit) + scrim behavior.
8. **Accessibility:** focus trap, ARIA roles, Esc-to-close, scrim-dismiss rules, min tap targets.
9. **Voice/tone** ("neighbor" voice) + copy patterns.
10. **Reusable component:** one shared modal component per guide, injected via the existing component-marker pattern, so every modal is one implementation.

## Deliverables

* Written standard (one doc per guide).
* Reusable modal component implemented in each surface's prototype.
* Existing ad-hoc modals migrated to the standard (inventory + convert).

## Acceptance

* Both guides documented and approved.
* A reusable modal component exists and is used by all modals in Request, Connect, and both apps.
* No modal derives its visual design from old Figma.
* **This ticket is a HARD BLOCKER:** no groomed ticket is handed to the developer until the modal standards are built and implemented. Tickets whose UI includes a modal (e.g. G40-137's "Counter-Offer Update") consume this standard rather than any Figma frame.

## Note on existing handoffs

Groomed tickets that referenced a Figma modal (notably **G40-137**) are updated to point their modal UI at this standard; the old Figma node is retained only as intent/copy reference, not as visual design.
